"""The one-time import of an old list, such as my-todos.txt, with one task per line.

A line can start with [ ] or [x], and can hold a due date written as (due YYYY-MM-DD), #tags, and at its end
a weekday word such as fri or a repeat hint: every day, every week or every monday. A weekday means the next
such day, never today. A line that cannot be read as it is gets left out with its reason: nothing is guessed.
"""
import datetime
import re

from jotdown import tasks

WEEKDAYS = ["monday", "tuesday", "wednesday", "thursday", "friday", "saturday", "sunday"]
DAY_NUMBERS = {**{name: n for n, name in enumerate(WEEKDAYS)}, **{name[:3]: n for n, name in enumerate(WEEKDAYS)}}

BOX = re.compile(r"^\[([ xX])\]\s*")
DUE = re.compile(r"\(due (\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})\)")
TAG = re.compile(r"(?<!\S)#([\w-]+)")
EVERY = re.compile(r"\s+every (day|week|" + "|".join(WEEKDAYS) + r")$", re.IGNORECASE)
LAST_DAY = re.compile(r"\s+(" + "|".join(DAY_NUMBERS) + r")$", re.IGNORECASE)


class LineError(Exception):
    """A line the import cannot take as it is. The message is the reason."""


def next_weekday(number, today):
    """The next day with that weekday number, never today."""
    return today + datetime.timedelta(days=(number - today.weekday()) % 7 or 7)


def read_line(line, today):
    """Read one line into a task's fields. Raises LineError for a line that cannot be read as it is."""
    text = line.strip()
    done = False
    box = BOX.match(text)
    if box:
        done = box.group(1) != " "
        text = text[box.end():]
    due = None
    found = DUE.search(text)
    if found:
        try:
            due = datetime.date.fromisoformat(found.group(1))
        except ValueError:
            raise LineError(f"{found.group(1)} is not a real date") from None
        text = text[:found.start()] + text[found.end():]
    tags = TAG.findall(text)
    text = " ".join(TAG.sub(" ", text).split())
    repeat = None
    every = EVERY.search(text)
    if every:
        word = every.group(1).lower()
        repeat = "daily" if word == "day" else "weekly"
        if word in DAY_NUMBERS and due is None:
            due = next_weekday(DAY_NUMBERS[word], today)
        text = text[:every.start()]
    else:
        day = LAST_DAY.search(text)
        if day and due is None:
            due = next_weekday(DAY_NUMBERS[day.group(1).lower()], today)
            text = text[:day.start()]
    title = text.strip()
    if not re.search(r"\w", title):
        raise LineError("not a task")
    return {"title": title, "done": done, "due": due, "tags": tags, "repeat": repeat}


def import_text(text, data, today):
    """Add a task to the list for each line. Returns (added, already there, left out).

    A line whose title is already a task in the list is not added again, so running the import twice adds
    nothing. Left out lines come back as (line number, line, reason).
    """
    known = {task["title"].casefold() for task in data["tasks"]}
    added = already = 0
    left_out = []
    for number, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), start=1):
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        try:
            fields = read_line(line, today)
        except LineError as error:
            left_out.append((number, line.strip(), str(error)))
            continue
        if fields["title"].casefold() in known:
            already += 1
            continue
        task = tasks.add_task(data, fields["title"], today=today, due=fields["due"], tags=fields["tags"],
                              repeat=fields["repeat"])
        task["done"] = fields["done"]
        known.add(fields["title"].casefold())
        added += 1
    return added, already, left_out

import datetime
import io
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from unittest import mock

from jotdown import cli
from jotdown.store import Store

TODAY = datetime.date(2027, 3, 15)


class CommandTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        folder = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(folder.cleanup)
        self.path = Path(folder.name) / "tasks.json"
        self.store = Store(self.path)

    def jd(self, *argv):
        out, err = io.StringIO(), io.StringIO()
        status = cli.main(list(argv), store=self.store, today=TODAY, out=out, err=err)
        return status, out.getvalue(), err.getvalue()

    def test_add_with_a_due_date_tags_and_a_repeat(self):
        status, out, _ = self.jd("add", "put", "the", "bins", "out", "--due", "2027-03-22",
                                 "--tag", "home", "--tag", "Chores", "--repeat", "weekly")
        self.assertEqual(status, 0)
        self.assertIn("Added 1. put the bins out", out)
        task = self.store.load()["tasks"][0]
        self.assertEqual((task["due"], task["tags"], task["repeat"]), ("2027-03-22", ["chores", "home"], "weekly"))

    def test_list_shows_the_open_tasks_and_one_tag_group(self):
        self.jd("add", "sow carrots", "--tag", "garden")
        self.jd("add", "book dentist", "--tag", "health")
        self.assertIn("sow carrots", self.jd("list")[1])
        _, out, _ = self.jd("list", "--tag", "garden")
        self.assertIn("sow carrots", out)
        self.assertNotIn("book dentist", out)

    def test_done_finishes_a_task_and_list_done_still_shows_it(self):
        self.jd("add", "fix bike")
        self.assertEqual(self.jd("done", "1")[:2], (0, "Done: 1. fix bike\n"))
        self.assertEqual(self.jd("list")[1], "No tasks.\n")
        self.assertIn("[x] 1. fix bike", self.jd("list", "--done")[1])

    def test_done_on_a_daily_task_three_days_late_shows_one_next_task_due_today(self):
        self.jd("add", "water the tomatoes", "--due", "2027-03-12", "--repeat", "daily")
        _, out, _ = self.jd("done", "1")
        self.assertIn("Next: 2. water the tomatoes (due 2027-03-15)", out)
        self.assertEqual(self.jd("list")[1].count("water the tomatoes"), 1)

    def test_edit_changes_one_repeating_task_unless_all_is_given(self):
        self.jd("add", "water the tomatoes", "--repeat", "daily")
        self.jd("edit", "1", "--title", "water the seedlings")
        self.assertIn("Next: 2. water the tomatoes", self.jd("done", "1")[1])
        self.jd("edit", "2", "--title", "water the seedlings", "--all")
        self.assertIn("Next: 3. water the seedlings", self.jd("done", "2")[1])

    def test_summary_is_what_jd_shows_with_no_command(self):
        self.jd("add", "pay council tax", "--due", "2027-03-10")
        _, summary, _ = self.jd("summary")
        self.assertEqual(self.jd()[1], summary)
        self.assertIn("Late", summary)

    def test_import_reads_a_file_lists_what_it_left_out_and_leaves_the_file_as_it_is(self):
        old = self.path.with_name("old-list.txt")
        old.write_text("[ ] renew passport (due 2027-03-31)\n[x] fix bike\n----\n", encoding="utf-8")
        status, out, _ = self.jd("import", str(old))
        self.assertEqual(status, 0)
        self.assertIn("Imported 2 tasks", out)
        self.assertIn("line 3: ---- (not a task)", out)
        self.assertEqual(old.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), "[ ] renew passport (due 2027-03-31)\n[x] fix bike\n----\n")
        self.assertEqual(self.jd("import", str(old))[1].splitlines()[0],
                         f"Imported 0 tasks from {old}. 2 were already in the list.")

    def test_web_starts_the_page_on_the_port_given(self):
        with mock.patch("jotdown.web.serve") as serve:
            status, _, _ = self.jd("web", "--port", "8800")
        self.assertEqual(status, 0)
        self.assertEqual(serve.call_args.args[:2], (self.store, 8800))

    def test_a_bad_date_or_task_number_is_an_error_not_a_crash(self):
        status, _, err = self.jd("add", "pay rent", "--due", "2027-02-30")
        self.assertEqual(status, 1)
        self.assertIn("2027-02-30", err)
        self.assertEqual(self.jd("done", "9")[0], 1)
        self.assertFalse(self.path.exists())

    def test_a_broken_data_file_stops_every_command_and_is_left_as_it_is(self):
        self.path.write_text("{not json", encoding="utf-8")
        for argv in (["list"], ["add", "fix bike"], ["done", "1"], ["edit", "1", "--title", "x"], ["summary"]):
            status, _, err = self.jd(*argv)
            self.assertEqual(status, 1)
            self.assertIn("left as it is", err)
        self.assertEqual(self.path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), "{not json")

import datetime
import unittest

from jotdown import importer
from jotdown.store import new_list

TODAY = datetime.date(2027, 3, 15)  # a Monday

SAMPLE = """[ ] renew passport (due 2027-03-31)
[x] fix bike
call mum fri #family
[ ] water the tomatoes every day #Garden
[ ] put the bins out every monday #home
[ ] plan the week every sunday
----
pay rent (due 2027-02-30)

[ ] book dentist #health
"""


class ImportTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.data = new_list()
        self.added, self.already, self.left_out = importer.import_text(SAMPLE, self.data, TODAY)
        self.by_title = {task["title"]: task for task in self.data["tasks"]}

    def fields(self, title):
        task = self.by_title[title]
        return task["done"], task["due"], task["tags"], task["repeat"]

    def test_a_box_and_a_due_date(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.fields("renew passport"), (False, "2027-03-31", [], None))

    def test_a_ticked_box_is_a_finished_task(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.fields("fix bike"), (True, None, [], None))

    def test_a_weekday_word_is_the_next_such_day_and_tags_are_kept(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.fields("call mum"), (False, "2027-03-19", ["family"], None))

    def test_every_day_is_a_daily_repeat_due_today_with_lowercase_tags(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.fields("water the tomatoes"), (False, "2027-03-15", ["garden"], "daily"))

    def test_every_weekday_is_a_weekly_repeat_due_on_the_next_such_day_never_today(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.fields("put the bins out"), (False, "2027-03-22", ["home"], "weekly"))
        self.assertEqual(self.fields("plan the week"), (False, "2027-03-21", [], "weekly"))

    def test_lines_it_cannot_take_are_left_out_with_their_reason_and_not_guessed(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.left_out, [(7, "----", "not a task"),
                                         (8, "pay rent (due 2027-02-30)", "2027-02-30 is not a real date")])
        self.assertNotIn("pay rent", self.by_title)

    def test_every_line_is_a_task_or_is_left_out(self):
        lines = [line for line in SAMPLE.splitlines() if line.strip()]
        self.assertEqual((self.added, self.already, len(self.left_out)), (7, 0, 2))
        self.assertEqual(self.added + len(self.left_out), len(lines))

    def test_running_the_import_twice_adds_nothing(self):
        again = importer.import_text(SAMPLE, self.data, TODAY)
        self.assertEqual(again[:2], (0, 7))
        self.assertEqual(len(self.data["tasks"]), 7)

import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path
source = Path("data/my-todos-original.txt")

unmatched = list(tasks)

"""The jd command."""
import argparse
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from jotdown import dates, importer, tasks, web
from jotdown.store import Store, StoreError


def build_parser():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="jd", description="Jotdown: a small task list.")
    commands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", metavar="COMMAND")

    add = commands.add_parser("add", help="add a task")
    add.add_argument("title", nargs="+")
    add.add_argument("--due", help='the due date, such as friday, "in 3 days" or 2027-03-19')
    add.add_argument("--tag", action="append", default=[], help="a tag; give it more than once for more tags")
    add.add_argument("--repeat", choices=sorted(tasks.REPEAT_DAYS))

    show = commands.add_parser("list", help="show the open tasks")
    show.add_argument("--tag", help="show one tag group")
    show.add_argument("--done", action="store_true", help="include finished tasks")

    done = commands.add_parser("done", help="finish a task")
    done.add_argument("id", type=int)

    edit = commands.add_parser("edit", help="change an open task")
    edit.add_argument("id", type=int)
    edit.add_argument("--title")
    edit.add_argument("--due", help='the new due date, such as friday, "in 3 days" or 2027-03-19')
    edit.add_argument("--tag", action="append", help="the new tags; give it more than once for more tags")
    edit.add_argument("--all", action="store_true", dest="all_repeats",
                      help="on a repeating task, change the tasks still to come as well")

    commands.add_parser("summary", help="show what is late and what is due today")

    load = commands.add_parser("import", help="read an old list, such as my-todos.txt, into the list")
    load.add_argument("file")

    page = commands.add_parser("web", help="start the page in the browser")
    page.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=web.DEFAULT_PORT)
    return parser


def cmd_add(args, store, today, out):
    due = dates.parse_due(args.due, today) if args.due else None
    data = store.load()
    task = tasks.add_task(data, " ".join(args.title), today=today, due=due, tags=args.tag, repeat=args.repeat)
    store.save(data)
    print(f"Added {tasks.format_task(task)}", file=out)
    return 0


def cmd_list(args, store, today, out):
    shown = tasks.visible_tasks(store.load(), args.tag, args.done)
    if not shown:
        print("No tasks.", file=out)
    for task in shown:
        print(("[x] " if task["done"] else "[ ] ") + tasks.format_task(task), file=out)
    return 0


def cmd_done(args, store, today, out):
    data = store.load()
    task, following = tasks.finish_task(data, args.id, today)
    store.save(data)
    print(f"Done: {tasks.format_task(task)}", file=out)
    if following:
        print(f"Next: {tasks.format_task(following)}", file=out)
    return 0


def cmd_edit(args, store, today, out):
    due = dates.parse_due(args.due, today) if args.due else None
    data = store.load()
    task = tasks.edit_task(data, args.id, title=args.title, due=due, tags=args.tag, all_repeats=args.all_repeats)
    store.save(data)
    print(f"Changed {tasks.format_task(task)}", file=out)
    return 0


def cmd_summary(args, store, today, out):
    print("\n".join(tasks.summary_lines(store.load(), today)), file=out)
    return 0


def cmd_import(args, store, today, out):
    try:
        text = Path(args.file).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    except OSError as error:
        raise tasks.TaskError(f"Cannot read {args.file}: {error.strerror}.") from None
    data = store.load()
    added, already, left_out = importer.import_text(text, data, today)
    store.save(data)
    print(f"Imported {added} tasks from {args.file}. {already} were already in the list.", file=out)
    if left_out:
        print(f"{len(left_out)} lines were left out:", file=out)
        for number, line, reason in left_out:
            print(f"  line {number}: {line} ({reason})", file=out)
    return 0


def cmd_web(args, store, today, out):
    web.serve(store, args.port, out)
    return 0


COMMANDS = {
    "add": cmd_add,
    "list": cmd_list,
    "done": cmd_done,
    "edit": cmd_edit,
    "summary": cmd_summary,
    "import": cmd_import,
    "web": cmd_web,
}


def main(argv=None, store=None, today=None, out=None, err=None):
    """Run one jd command and return its exit status. The keyword arguments are for tests."""
    out = out or sys.stdout
    err = err or sys.stderr
    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
    store = store or Store()
    today = today or dates.current_date()
    try:
        return COMMANDS[args.command or "summary"](args, store, today, out)
    except (tasks.TaskError, dates.DateError, StoreError) as error:
        print(f"jd: {error}", file=err)
        return 1

import datetime
import io
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from unittest import mock

from jotdown import cli
from jotdown.store import Store

TODAY = datetime.date(2027, 3, 15)


class CommandTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        folder = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(folder.cleanup)
        self.path = Path(folder.name) / "tasks.json"
        self.store = Store(self.path)

    def jd(self, *argv):
        out, err = io.StringIO(), io.StringIO()
        status = cli.main(list(argv), store=self.store, today=TODAY, out=out, err=err)
        return status, out.getvalue(), err.getvalue()

    def test_add_with_a_due_date_tags_and_a_repeat(self):
        status, out, _ = self.jd("add", "put", "the", "bins", "out", "--due", "2027-03-22",
                                 "--tag", "home", "--tag", "Chores", "--repeat", "weekly")
        self.assertEqual(status, 0)
        self.assertIn("Added 1. put the bins out", out)
        task = self.store.load()["tasks"][0]
        self.assertEqual((task["due"], task["tags"], task["repeat"]), ("2027-03-22", ["chores", "home"], "weekly"))

    def test_due_dates_in_plain_words(self):
        self.jd("add", "call mum", "--due", "friday")
        self.jd("add", "sow carrots", "--due", "in 3 days")
        self.jd("edit", "1", "--due", "fri")
        self.assertEqual([t["due"] for t in self.store.load()["tasks"]], ["2027-03-19", "2027-03-18"])

    def test_list_shows_the_open_tasks_and_one_tag_group(self):
        self.jd("add", "sow carrots", "--tag", "garden")
        self.jd("add", "book dentist", "--tag", "health")
        self.assertIn("sow carrots", self.jd("list")[1])
        _, out, _ = self.jd("list", "--tag", "garden")
        self.assertIn("sow carrots", out)
        self.assertNotIn("book dentist", out)

    def test_done_finishes_a_task_and_list_done_still_shows_it(self):
        self.jd("add", "fix bike")
        self.assertEqual(self.jd("done", "1")[:2], (0, "Done: 1. fix bike\n"))
        self.assertEqual(self.jd("list")[1], "No tasks.\n")
        self.assertIn("[x] 1. fix bike", self.jd("list", "--done")[1])

    def test_done_on_a_daily_task_three_days_late_shows_one_next_task_due_today(self):
        self.jd("add", "water the tomatoes", "--due", "2027-03-12", "--repeat", "daily")
        _, out, _ = self.jd("done", "1")
        self.assertIn("Next: 2. water the tomatoes (due 2027-03-15)", out)
        self.assertEqual(self.jd("list")[1].count("water the tomatoes"), 1)

    def test_edit_changes_one_repeating_task_unless_all_is_given(self):
        self.jd("add", "water the tomatoes", "--repeat", "daily")
        self.jd("edit", "1", "--title", "water the seedlings")
        self.assertIn("Next: 2. water the tomatoes", self.jd("done", "1")[1])
        self.jd("edit", "2", "--title", "water the seedlings", "--all")
        self.assertIn("Next: 3. water the seedlings", self.jd("done", "2")[1])

    def test_summary_is_what_jd_shows_with_no_command(self):
        self.jd("add", "pay council tax", "--due", "2027-03-10")
        _, summary, _ = self.jd("summary")
        self.assertEqual(self.jd()[1], summary)
        self.assertIn("Late", summary)

    def test_import_reads_a_file_lists_what_it_left_out_and_leaves_the_file_as_it_is(self):
        old = self.path.with_name("old-list.txt")
        old.write_text("[ ] renew passport (due 2027-03-31)\n[x] fix bike\n----\n", encoding="utf-8")
        status, out, _ = self.jd("import", str(old))
        self.assertEqual(status, 0)
        self.assertIn("Imported 2 tasks", out)
        self.assertIn("line 3: ---- (not a task)", out)
        self.assertEqual(old.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), "[ ] renew passport (due 2027-03-31)\n[x] fix bike\n----\n")
        self.assertEqual(self.jd("import", str(old))[1].splitlines()[0],
                         f"Imported 0 tasks from {old}. 2 were already in the list.")

    def test_web_starts_the_page_on_the_port_given(self):
        with mock.patch("jotdown.web.serve") as serve:
            status, _, _ = self.jd("web", "--port", "8800")
        self.assertEqual(status, 0)
        self.assertEqual(serve.call_args.args[:2], (self.store, 8800))

    def test_a_bad_date_or_task_number_is_an_error_not_a_crash(self):
        status, _, err = self.jd("add", "pay rent", "--due", "2027-02-30")
        self.assertEqual(status, 1)
        self.assertIn("2027-02-30", err)
        self.assertEqual(self.jd("done", "9")[0], 1)
        self.assertFalse(self.path.exists())

    def test_a_broken_data_file_stops_every_command_and_is_left_as_it_is(self):
        self.path.write_text("{not json", encoding="utf-8")
        for argv in (["list"], ["add", "fix bike"], ["done", "1"], ["edit", "1", "--title", "x"], ["summary"]):
            status, _, err = self.jd(*argv)
            self.assertEqual(status, 1)
            self.assertIn("left as it is", err)
        self.assertEqual(self.path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), "{not json")

import datetime
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

from jotdown import tasks
from jotdown.store import Store
from jotdown.web import HOST, Page

TODAY = datetime.date(2027, 3, 15)


class PageTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        folder = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(folder.cleanup)
        self.path = Path(folder.name) / "tasks.json"
        self.store = Store(self.path)
        self.page = Page(self.store, today=TODAY)

    def get(self, path="/"):
        status, headers, body = self.page.handle("GET", path, {})
        return status, headers, body.decode("utf-8")

    def post(self, path, form):
        return self.page.handle("POST", path, {}, form.encode("utf-8"))

    def test_the_page_listens_on_this_computer_only(self):
        self.assertEqual(HOST, "127.0.0.1")

    def test_an_empty_list_still_shows_the_page_and_the_summary(self):
        status, headers, body = self.get()
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(headers["Content-Type"], "text/html; charset=utf-8")
        self.assertIn("Nothing is late or due today.", body)
        self.assertIn('action="/add"', body)

    def test_adding_a_task_from_the_form_saves_it_and_shows_it(self):
        status, headers, _ = self.post("/add", "title=renew+passport&due=2027-03-31&tags=Admin")
        self.assertEqual((status, headers["Location"]), (303, "/"))
        task = self.store.load()["tasks"][0]
        self.assertEqual((task["title"], task["due"], task["tags"]), ("renew passport", "2027-03-31", ["admin"]))
        self.assertIn("renew passport", self.get()[2])

    def test_the_form_takes_due_dates_in_plain_words(self):
        self.post("/add", "title=call+mum&due=friday")
        self.post("/add", "title=sow+carrots&due=in+3+days")
        self.assertEqual([t["due"] for t in self.store.load()["tasks"]], ["2027-03-19", "2027-03-18"])

    def test_finishing_a_task_marks_it_done_and_takes_it_off_the_page(self):
        self.post("/add", "title=fix+bike")
        self.assertEqual(self.post("/done", "id=1")[0], 303)
        self.assertTrue(self.store.load()["tasks"][0]["done"])
        self.assertNotIn("fix bike", self.get()[2])

    def test_finishing_a_repeating_task_adds_the_next_one(self):
        self.post("/add", "title=water+the+tomatoes&repeat=daily")
        self.post("/done", "id=1")
        self.assertEqual([(t["id"], t["done"], t["due"]) for t in self.store.load()["tasks"]],
                         [(1, True, "2027-03-15"), (2, False, "2027-03-16")])

    def test_late_tasks_and_tasks_due_today_are_in_the_summary(self):
        self.post("/add", "title=pay+council+tax&due=2027-03-10")
        self.post("/add", "title=call+mum&due=2027-03-15")
        body = self.get()[2]
        self.assertIn("Late", body)
        self.assertIn("Due today", body)

    def test_a_task_added_by_a_command_shows_at_the_next_request(self):
        self.get()
        data = Store(self.path).load()
        tasks.add_task(data, "book dentist", today=TODAY)
        Store(self.path).save(data)
        self.assertIn("book dentist", self.get()[2])

    def test_a_bad_due_date_is_refused_and_nothing_is_saved(self):
        status, _, body = self.post("/add", "title=pay+rent&due=2027-02-30")
        self.assertEqual(status, 400)
        self.assertIn("2027-02-30", body.decode("utf-8"))
        self.assertFalse(self.path.exists())

    def test_an_unknown_or_missing_task_number_is_refused(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.post("/done", "id=7")[0], 400)
        self.assertEqual(self.post("/done", "id=seven")[0], 400)

    def test_titles_are_escaped(self):
        self.post("/add", "title=%3Cscript%3Ealert(1)%3C%2Fscript%3E")
        body = self.get()[2]
        self.assertIn("<script>", body)
        self.assertNotIn("<script>alert", body)

    def test_a_broken_data_file_stops_the_page_and_is_left_as_it_is(self):
        self.path.write_text("{not json", encoding="utf-8")
        status, _, body = self.get()
        self.assertEqual(status, 500)
        self.assertIn("left as it is", body)
        self.assertEqual(self.post("/add", "title=fix+bike")[0], 500)
        self.assertEqual(self.path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), "{not json")

    def test_another_address_is_not_found(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.get("/elsewhere")[0], 404)

import unittest
from pathlib import Path

import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

from jotdown import tasks
from jotdown.store import Store
from jotdown.web import HOST, Page

TODAY = datetime.date(2027, 3, 15)


class PageTests(unittest.TestCase):

        self.path = Path(folder.name) / "tasks.json"
        self.store = Store(self.path)
        self.page = Page(self.store, today=TODAY)

    def get(self, path="/"):
        status, headers, body = self.page.handle("GET", path, {})
        return status, headers, body.decode("utf-8")

    def post(self, path, form):
        return self.page.handle("POST", path, {}, form.encode("utf-8"))

    def test_the_page_listens_on_this_computer_only(self):
        self.assertEqual(HOST, "127.0.0.1")

    def test_an_empty_list_still_shows_the_page_and_the_summary(self):
        status, headers, body = self.get()
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(headers["Content-Type"], "text/html; charset=utf-8")
        self.assertIn("Nothing is late or due today.", body)
        self.assertIn('action="/add"', body)

    def test_adding_a_task_from_the_form_saves_it_and_shows_it(self):
        status, headers, _ = self.post("/add", "title=renew+passport&due=2027-03-31&tags=Admin")
        self.assertEqual((status, headers["Location"]), (303, "/"))
        task = self.store.load()["tasks"][0]
        self.assertEqual((task["title"], task["due"], task["tags"]), ("renew passport", "2027-03-31", ["admin"]))
        self.assertIn("renew passport", self.get()[2])

    def test_the_form_takes_due_dates_in_plain_words(self):
        self.post("/add", "title=call+mum&due=friday")
        self.post("/add", "title=sow+carrots&due=in+3+days")
        self.assertEqual([t["due"] for t in self.store.load()["tasks"]], ["2027-03-19", "2027-03-18"])

    def test_finishing_a_task_marks_it_done_and_takes_it_off_the_page(self):
        self.post("/add", "title=fix+bike")
        self.assertEqual(self.post("/done", "id=1")[0], 303)
        self.assertTrue(self.store.load()["tasks"][0]["done"])
        self.assertNotIn("fix bike", self.get()[2])

    def test_finishing_a_repeating_task_adds_the_next_one(self):
        self.post("/add", "title=water+the+tomatoes&repeat=daily")
        self.post("/done", "id=1")
        self.assertEqual([(t["id"], t["done"], t["due"]) for t in self.store.load()["tasks"]],
                         [(1, True, "2027-03-15"), (2, False, "2027-03-16")])

    def test_late_tasks_and_tasks_due_today_are_in_the_summary(self):
        self.post("/add", "title=pay+council+tax&due=2027-03-10")

        body = self.get()[2]
        self.assertIn("Late", body)
        self.assertIn("Due today", body)

        Store(self.path).save(data)
        self.assertIn("book dentist", self.get()[2])

        self.assertIn("2027-02-30", body.decode("utf-8"))
        self.assertFalse(self.path.exists())

    def test_an_unknown_or_missing_task_number_is_refused(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.post("/done", "id=7")[0], 400)
        self.assertEqual(self.post("/done", "id=seven")[0], 400)

    def test_titles_are_escaped(self):
        self.post("/add", "title=%3Cscript%3Ealert(1)%3C%2Fscript%3E")

        self.assertEqual(self.post("/add", "title=fix+bike")[0], 500)
        self.assertEqual(self.path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), "{not json")

    def test_another_address_is_not_found(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.get("/elsewhere")[0], 404)

import argparse
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from jotdown import dates, importer, tasks, web
from jotdown.store import Store, StoreError


def build_parser():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="jd", description="Jotdown: a small task list.")
    commands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", metavar="COMMAND")

    add = commands.add_parser("add", help="add a task")
    add.add_argument("title", nargs="+")
    add.add_argument("--due", help='the due date, such as friday, "in 3 days" or 2027-03-19')
    add.add_argument("--tag", action="append", default=[], help="a tag; give it more than once for more tags")
    add.add_argument("--repeat", choices=sorted(tasks.REPEAT_DAYS))

    show = commands.add_parser("list", help="show the open tasks")
    show.add_argument("--tag", help="show one tag group")
    show.add_argument("--done", action="store_true", help="include finished tasks")

    done = commands.add_parser("done", help="finish a task")
    done.add_argument("id", type=int)

    edit = commands.add_parser("edit", help="change an open task")
    edit.add_argument("id", type=int)
    edit.add_argument("--title")
    edit.add_argument("--due", help='the new due date, such as friday, "in 3 days" or 2027-03-19')
    edit.add_argument("--tag", action="append", help="the new tags; give it more than once for more tags")
    edit.add_argument("--all", action="store_true", dest="all_repeats",
                      help="on a repeating task, change the tasks still to come as well")

    commands.add_parser("summary", help="show what is late and what is due today")
    commands.add_parser("today", help="count the tasks due today")

    load = commands.add_parser("import", help="read an old list, such as my-todos.txt, into the list")
    load.add_argument("file")

    page = commands.add_parser("web", help="start the page in the browser")
    page.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=web.DEFAULT_PORT)
    return parser


def cmd_add(args, store, today, out):
    due = dates.parse_due(args.due, today) if args.due else None
    data = store.load()
    task = tasks.add_task(data, " ".join(args.title), today=today, due=due, tags=args.tag, repeat=args.repeat)
    store.save(data)
    print(f"Added {tasks.format_task(task)}", file=out)
    return 0


def cmd_list(args, store, today, out):
    shown = tasks.visible_tasks(store.load(), args.tag, args.done)
    if not shown:
        print("No tasks.", file=out)
    for task in shown:
        print(("[x] " if task["done"] else "[ ] ") + tasks.format_task(task), file=out)
    return 0


def cmd_done(args, store, today, out):
    data = store.load()
    task, following = tasks.finish_task(data, args.id, today)
    store.save(data)
    print(f"Done: {tasks.format_task(task)}", file=out)
    if following:
        print(f"Next: {tasks.format_task(following)}", file=out)
    return 0


def cmd_edit(args, store, today, out):
    due = dates.parse_due(args.due, today) if args.due else None
    data = store.load()
    task = tasks.edit_task(data, args.id, title=args.title, due=due, tags=args.tag, all_repeats=args.all_repeats)
    store.save(data)
    print(f"Changed {tasks.format_task(task)}", file=out)
    return 0


def cmd_summary(args, store, today, out):
    print("\n".join(tasks.summary_lines(store.load(), today)), file=out)
    return 0


def cmd_import(args, store, today, out):
    try:
        text = Path(args.file).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    except OSError as error:
        raise tasks.TaskError(f"Cannot read {args.file}: {error.strerror}.") from None
    data = store.load()
    added, already, left_out = importer.import_text(text, data, today)
    store.save(data)
    print(f"Imported {added} tasks from {args.file}. {already} were already in the list.", file=out)
    if left_out:
        print(f"{len(left_out)} lines were left out:", file=out)
        for number, line, reason in left_out:
            print(f"  line {number}: {line} ({reason})", file=out)
    return 0


def cmd_today(args, store, today, out):
    due = [t for t in store.load()["tasks"] if not t["done"] and t["due"] == today.isoformat()]
    print(f"{len(due)} tasks due today", file=out)
    return 0


def cmd_web(args, store, today, out):
    web.serve(store, args.port, out)
    return 0


COMMANDS = {
    "add": cmd_add,
    "list": cmd_list,
    "done": cmd_done,
    "edit": cmd_edit,
    "summary": cmd_summary,
    "today": cmd_today,
    "import": cmd_import,
    "web": cmd_web,
}


def main(argv=None, store=None, today=None, out=None, err=None):
    """Run one jd command and return its exit status. The keyword arguments are for tests."""
    out = out or sys.stdout
    err = err or sys.stderr
    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
    store = store or Store()
    today = today or dates.current_date()
    try:
        return COMMANDS[args.command or "summary"](args, store, today, out)
    except (tasks.TaskError, dates.DateError, StoreError) as error:
        print(f"jd: {error}", file=err)
        return 1

import datetime
import io
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from unittest import mock

from jotdown import cli
from jotdown.store import Store

TODAY = datetime.date(2027, 3, 15)


class CommandTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        folder = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(folder.cleanup)
        self.path = Path(folder.name) / "tasks.json"
        self.store = Store(self.path)

    def jd(self, *argv):
        out, err = io.StringIO(), io.StringIO()
        status = cli.main(list(argv), store=self.store, today=TODAY, out=out, err=err)
        return status, out.getvalue(), err.getvalue()

    def test_add_with_a_due_date_tags_and_a_repeat(self):
        status, out, _ = self.jd("add", "put", "the", "bins", "out", "--due", "2027-03-22",
                                 "--tag", "home", "--tag", "Chores", "--repeat", "weekly")
        self.assertEqual(status, 0)
        self.assertIn("Added 1. put the bins out", out)
        task = self.store.load()["tasks"][0]
        self.assertEqual((task["due"], task["tags"], task["repeat"]), ("2027-03-22", ["chores", "home"], "weekly"))

    def test_due_dates_in_plain_words(self):
        self.jd("add", "call mum", "--due", "friday")
        self.jd("add", "sow carrots", "--due", "in 3 days")
        self.jd("edit", "1", "--due", "fri")
        self.assertEqual([t["due"] for t in self.store.load()["tasks"]], ["2027-03-19", "2027-03-18"])

    def test_list_shows_the_open_tasks_and_one_tag_group(self):
        self.jd("add", "sow carrots", "--tag", "garden")
        self.jd("add", "book dentist", "--tag", "health")
        self.assertIn("sow carrots", self.jd("list")[1])
        _, out, _ = self.jd("list", "--tag", "garden")
        self.assertIn("sow carrots", out)
        self.assertNotIn("book dentist", out)

    def test_done_finishes_a_task_and_list_done_still_shows_it(self):
        self.jd("add", "fix bike")
        self.assertEqual(self.jd("done", "1")[:2], (0, "Done: 1. fix bike\n"))
        self.assertEqual(self.jd("list")[1], "No tasks.\n")
        self.assertIn("[x] 1. fix bike", self.jd("list", "--done")[1])

    def test_done_on_a_daily_task_three_days_late_shows_one_next_task_due_today(self):
        self.jd("add", "water the tomatoes", "--due", "2027-03-12", "--repeat", "daily")
        _, out, _ = self.jd("done", "1")
        self.assertIn("Next: 2. water the tomatoes (due 2027-03-15)", out)
        self.assertEqual(self.jd("list")[1].count("water the tomatoes"), 1)

    def test_edit_changes_one_repeating_task_unless_all_is_given(self):
        self.jd("add", "water the tomatoes", "--repeat", "daily")
        self.jd("edit", "1", "--title", "water the seedlings")
        self.assertIn("Next: 2. water the tomatoes", self.jd("done", "1")[1])
        self.jd("edit", "2", "--title", "water the seedlings", "--all")
        self.assertIn("Next: 3. water the seedlings", self.jd("done", "2")[1])

    def test_summary_is_what_jd_shows_with_no_command(self):
        self.jd("add", "pay council tax", "--due", "2027-03-10")
        _, summary, _ = self.jd("summary")
        self.assertEqual(self.jd()[1], summary)
        self.assertIn("Late", summary)

    def test_import_reads_a_file_lists_what_it_left_out_and_leaves_the_file_as_it_is(self):
        old = self.path.with_name("old-list.txt")
        old.write_text("[ ] renew passport (due 2027-03-31)\n[x] fix bike\n----\n", encoding="utf-8")
        status, out, _ = self.jd("import", str(old))
        self.assertEqual(status, 0)
        self.assertIn("Imported 2 tasks", out)
        self.assertIn("line 3: ---- (not a task)", out)
        self.assertEqual(old.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), "[ ] renew passport (due 2027-03-31)\n[x] fix bike\n----\n")
        self.assertEqual(self.jd("import", str(old))[1].splitlines()[0],
                         f"Imported 0 tasks from {old}. 2 were already in the list.")

    def test_web_starts_the_page_on_the_port_given(self):
        with mock.patch("jotdown.web.serve") as serve:
            status, _, _ = self.jd("web", "--port", "8800")
        self.assertEqual(status, 0)
        self.assertEqual(serve.call_args.args[:2], (self.store, 8800))

    def test_a_bad_date_or_task_number_is_an_error_not_a_crash(self):
        status, _, err = self.jd("add", "pay rent", "--due", "2027-02-30")
        self.assertEqual(status, 1)
        self.assertIn("2027-02-30", err)
        self.assertEqual(self.jd("done", "9")[0], 1)
        self.assertFalse(self.path.exists())

    def test_a_broken_data_file_stops_every_command_and_is_left_as_it_is(self):
        self.path.write_text("{not json", encoding="utf-8")
        for argv in (["list"], ["add", "fix bike"], ["done", "1"], ["edit", "1", "--title", "x"], ["summary"]):
            status, _, err = self.jd(*argv)
            self.assertEqual(status, 1)
            self.assertIn("left as it is", err)
        self.assertEqual(self.path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), "{not json")

import datetime
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

from jotdown import tasks
from jotdown.store import Store
from jotdown.web import HOST, Page

TODAY = datetime.date(2027, 3, 15)


class PageTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        folder = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(folder.cleanup)
        self.path = Path(folder.name) / "tasks.json"
        self.store = Store(self.path)
        self.page = Page(self.store, today=TODAY)

    def get(self, path="/"):
        status, headers, body = self.page.handle("GET", path, {})
        return status, headers, body.decode("utf-8")

    def post(self, path, form):
        return self.page.handle("POST", path, {}, form.encode("utf-8"))

    def test_the_page_listens_on_this_computer_only(self):
        self.assertEqual(HOST, "127.0.0.1")

    def test_an_empty_list_still_shows_the_page_and_the_summary(self):
        status, headers, body = self.get()
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(headers["Content-Type"], "text/html; charset=utf-8")
        self.assertIn("Nothing is late or due today.", body)
        self.assertIn('action="/add"', body)

    def test_adding_a_task_from_the_form_saves_it_and_shows_it(self):
        status, headers, _ = self.post("/add", "title=renew+passport&due=2027-03-31&tags=Admin")
        self.assertEqual((status, headers["Location"]), (303, "/"))
        task = self.store.load()["tasks"][0]
        self.assertEqual((task["title"], task["due"], task["tags"]), ("renew passport", "2027-03-31", ["admin"]))
        self.assertIn("renew passport", self.get()[2])

    def test_the_form_takes_due_dates_in_plain_words(self):
        self.post("/add", "title=call+mum&due=friday")
        self.post("/add", "title=sow+carrots&due=in+3+days")
        self.assertEqual([t["due"] for t in self.store.load()["tasks"]], ["2027-03-19", "2027-03-18"])

    def test_finishing_a_task_marks_it_done_and_takes_it_off_the_page(self):
        self.post("/add", "title=fix+bike")
        self.assertEqual(self.post("/done", "id=1")[0], 303)
        self.assertTrue(self.store.load()["tasks"][0]["done"])
        self.assertNotIn("fix bike", self.get()[2])

    def test_finishing_a_repeating_task_adds_the_next_one(self):
        self.post("/add", "title=water+the+tomatoes&repeat=daily")
        self.post("/done", "id=1")
        self.assertEqual([(t["id"], t["done"], t["due"]) for t in self.store.load()["tasks"]],
                         [(1, True, "2027-03-15"), (2, False, "2027-03-16")])

    def test_late_tasks_and_tasks_due_today_are_in_the_summary(self):
        self.post("/add", "title=pay+council+tax&due=2027-03-10")
        self.post("/add", "title=call+mum&due=2027-03-15")
        body = self.get()[2]
        self.assertIn("Late", body)
        self.assertIn("Due today", body)

    def test_a_task_added_by_a_command_shows_at_the_next_request(self):
        self.get()
        data = Store(self.path).load()
        tasks.add_task(data, "book dentist", today=TODAY)
        Store(self.path).save(data)
        self.assertIn("book dentist", self.get()[2])

    def test_a_bad_due_date_is_refused_and_nothing_is_saved(self):
        status, _, body = self.post("/add", "title=pay+rent&due=2027-02-30")
        self.assertEqual(status, 400)
        self.assertIn("2027-02-30", body.decode("utf-8"))
        self.assertFalse(self.path.exists())

    def test_an_unknown_or_missing_task_number_is_refused(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.post("/done", "id=7")[0], 400)
        self.assertEqual(self.post("/done", "id=seven")[0], 400)

    def test_titles_are_escaped(self):
        self.post("/add", "title=%3Cscript%3Ealert(1)%3C%2Fscript%3E")
        body = self.get()[2]
        self.assertIn("<script>", body)
        self.assertNotIn("<script>alert", body)

    def test_a_broken_data_file_stops_the_page_and_is_left_as_it_is(self):
        self.path.write_text("{not json", encoding="utf-8")
        status, _, body = self.get()
        self.assertEqual(status, 500)
        self.assertIn("left as it is", body)
        self.assertEqual(self.post("/add", "title=fix+bike")[0], 500)
        self.assertEqual(self.path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), "{not json")

    def test_another_address_is_not_found(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.get("/elsewhere")[0], 404)

def cmd_import(args, store, today, out):

    except OSError as error:
        raise tasks.TaskError(f"Cannot read {args.file}: {error.strerror}.") from None
    data = store.load()
    added, already, left_out = importer.import_text(text, data, today)
    store.save(data)
    print(f"Imported {added} tasks from {args.file}. {already} were already in the list.", file=out)
    if left_out:
        print(f"{len(left_out)} lines were left out:", file=out)
        for number, line, reason in left_out:
            print(f"  line {number}: {line} ({reason})", file=out)
    return 0

    return 0

    "list": cmd_list,
    "done": cmd_done,
    "edit": cmd_edit,
    "summary": cmd_summary,
    "import": cmd_import,
    "web": cmd_web,
}


def main(argv=None, store=None, today=None, out=None, err=None):
    """Run one jd command and return its exit status. The keyword arguments are for tests."""
    out = out or sys.stdout
    err = err or sys.stderr
    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
    store = store or Store()
    today = today or dates.current_date()
    try:
        return COMMANDS[args.command or "summary"](args, store, today, out)
    except (tasks.TaskError, dates.DateError, StoreError) as error:
        print(f"jd: {error}", file=err)
        return 1

        self.assertIn('action="/add"', body)

        status, headers, _ = self.post("/add", "title=renew+passport&due=2027-03-31&tags=Admin")
        self.assertEqual((status, headers["Location"]), (303, "/"))
        task = self.store.load()["tasks"][0]
        self.assertEqual((task["title"], task["due"], task["tags"]), ("renew passport", "2027-03-31", ["admin"]))

        self.assertEqual(self.get("/elsewhere")[0], 404)

Written on Monday 15 March 2027, against branch `main` at commit a3c9e51. A fresh reader with none of the conversation behind it read this note cold; its questions are answered below. The owner has not approved it yet. Read it whole before you act on it.

## Goal and state

Jotdown is a small task list in Python's standard library: the `jd` commands and a page in the browser that only the same computer can reach. Steps 5, the README, and 6, a friend installs it, are not started.

## Structure and concepts

- `DESIGN.md`: the approved design: the store, the commands, the page, the import, repeats and the file format.

- `decisions.md`: everything settled, with the repeat rules under "Repeat rules".
- `glossary.md`: the words to use: task, list, tag, tag group, due date and repeat. Not "todo" or "item".

- `vendor/tinydate/`: a small date reader by someone else, used as it is.
- `questions-for-friends.md`: the questions for the friends. No answers have come back.

- `AGENTS.md` holds the project's rules: work only in this project; no network; never push, publish, send email or use real accounts; Python's standard library only, and ask before installing anything; the test command `python3 -m unittest`.

- `AGENTS.md` gives the project's reference date; treat it as today.

- Recorded in `DESIGN.md`, `decisions.md` and `plan.md`: everything not listed below.

  - `data/tasks.json` lives in the project folder, found from the code's own location, so running from another folder uses the same list. `DESIGN.md` does not say what the path is relative to. Where the list lives once Jotdown is installed is still open.

# Jotdown

A small task list for the command line and for a page in your browser. It needs Python 3.12 or newer and nothing else.

## Install

1. Install Python 3.12 or newer.
2. Copy the Jotdown folder to your computer.
3. In that folder, run `python3 -m jotdown` to check that it starts.

## Use

```text
jd add "renew passport" --due 2027-03-31 --tag admin
jd list
jd done 1
jd web
```

Run `jd` with no command to see what is late and what is due today.

## Licence

Jotdown is released under the MIT licence.

## How to fix the vanished tasks

The cause is almost certainly jotdown/store.py line 7, `DATA_PATH = Path("data") / "tasks.json"`: the path is relative, so `jd` looks for data/ inside whatever folder it runs in. The fix is to build it from the home folder instead:

```python
def default_path():
    return Path.home() / ".jotdown" / "tasks.json"
```

observation.final_answer:
Sam and Priya each got "No tasks.", with no error, the first time they ran `jd list` from a different folder than the one where they had added their tasks; since when is unknown. Their tasks aren't lost. `jd` keeps the list in a `data/tasks.json` inside whatever folder it runs in, so running it from another folder starts a new, empty list, and the tasks are still in the folder where they were added. I confirmed this by reproducing it in a scratch folder. I fixed and changed nothing.

## What happened

- Sam (friends/reports.md line 7): he added tasks on Friday in `/home/sam/work`. This morning `jd list`, run from his home folder, said "No tasks."
- Priya (lines 11–14): she added about a dozen tasks in `C:\Users\Priya\Documents\jotdown`. Later, in a new window that starts in `C:\Users\Priya`, `jd list` said "No tasks."
- Both saw it the first time they ran `jd` from a different folder than the one where they added the tasks. No error, only "No tasks."
- Leo always starts it from the same folder and has had no problem (line 20): the working case.
- Since when: unknown. The reports, collected on 9 April (line 3), don't say.

## The cause, confirmed by reproducing it

I tested one cause: the list is looked up relative to the folder `jd` runs in. In a scratch folder outside the project, with two empty folders, `first` and `other`, I ran the project's own code:

1. In `first`: `jd add "probe task"` printed "Added [1] probe task", and `jd list` showed it.
2. In `other`: `jd list` printed "No tasks.", the friends' symptom. `other` had no `data/` folder.
3. In `other`: `jd add "second probe"` printed "Added [1] second probe" and created `other/data/tasks.json`. Back in `first`, `jd list` still showed "probe task".

So each folder gets a list of its own, and the first folder's list stays as it was.

## The chain back to where it starts

1. The command opens the store without a path: jotdown/cli.py line 121, `store = store or Store()`.
2. The store then uses `DATA_PATH = Path("data") / "tasks.json"` (jotdown/store.py lines 7 and 16). That path is relative, so it is read from the folder `jd` runs in, as the probe shows.
3. With no file there, the store returns a new, empty list (store.py lines 22–23): hence "No tasks." and no error.
4. It starts in the design: DESIGN.md line 29 says "The list is kept in `data/tasks.json`" without saying relative to what, and the code follows it.

## Ruled out

- A broken data file: the probe gave the same "No tasks." with no broken file anywhere; the file was simply missing.
- Something deleting the list: nothing in jotdown/ removes a file (I searched it for file removal), and the first folder's list survived the probe.

## Their tasks are still there

They should be in the folders where they were added: `/home/sam/work/data/tasks.json` for Sam and `C:\Users\Priya\Documents\jotdown\data\tasks.json` for Priya. `jd list` run from that folder should show them again. I haven't seen their computers; this follows from the reproduction.

## Where a fix belongs

Where it starts: the design should name one place for the list that doesn't depend on the current folder, and the store should use it. I haven't changed anything, as you asked.

"""Shows that the list depends on the folder jd runs in."""
import os
import tempfile
import unittest

from jotdown.store import Store, new_data


class FolderProbeTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_other_folder_sees_no_tasks(self):
        start = os.getcwd()
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as first, tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as other:
            try:
                os.chdir(first)
                data = new_data()
                data["tasks"].append({"id": 1, "title": "probe"})
                Store().save(data)
                os.chdir(other)
                self.assertEqual(Store().load()["tasks"], [])
            finally:
                os.chdir(start)

# Jotdown design

Status: approved on 8 March 2027, with the reviewer's findings fixed.

## Purpose

Jotdown is a small task list for the command line and for a page in the browser. It is for its owner first and then for three friends, Sam, Priya and Leo, each on their own computer. Version 1 uses Python's standard library only.

## Scope

In version 1:

- tasks with a due date, tags and a daily or weekly repeat;
- commands to add, list, finish and edit tasks;
- a page in the browser that lists tasks, adds them and finishes them;
- a summary of late tasks and tasks due today, shown when the app opens;
- a one-time import of `my-todos.txt`.

Not in version 1: sharing or sync between people, a phone app, email reminders, and deleting tasks. To drop a task, finish it, or edit the file by hand.

## Words

The words are the ones in `glossary.md`: task, list, tag, tag group, due date and repeat. The commands, the page and the code use no other word for these things.

## Parts

### The store

The store reads and saves the list. The list is kept in one file, `~/.jotdown/tasks.json`: a `.jotdown` folder in the user's home folder, such as `/home/sam/.jotdown/tasks.json` or `C:\Users\Priya\.jotdown\tasks.json`. The folder the command runs in does not matter: every command and the page use this one file.

A save writes the whole list to a new file beside the old one, then renames the new file over the old one. A save that is cut off leaves the old file whole.

A missing file means a new, empty list. A file that exists but cannot be read as a list is an error: the store stops and says so. It never carries on with an empty list, because the next save would overwrite the file.

### The commands

The command is `jd`. With no command it shows the summary.

- `jd add TITLE`, with `--due`, `--tag` (more than once is fine) and `--repeat daily|weekly`.
- `jd list`, with `--tag` to show one tag group and `--done` to include finished tasks.
- `jd done ID` finishes a task.
- `jd edit ID`, with `--title`, `--due`, `--tag` and `--all`.
- `jd summary` shows what is late and what is due today.
- `jd import FILE` reads an old list.
- `jd web` starts the page.

### The page

`jd web` starts a page that listens on 127.0.0.1, the computer's own address, so only that computer can reach it. It shows the summary, lists the open tasks, adds a task from a form and finishes a task with a button. It uses `http.server` from the standard library.

### The import

`jd import FILE` reads a file such as `my-todos.txt`, one task per line. It takes `[ ]` and `[x]` at the start, a due date written as `(due YYYY-MM-DD)`, `#tags`, a weekday word such as `fri`, and the hints `every day`, `every week` and `every monday`. A line it cannot read as it is gets left out and listed with the reason. It never guesses. Running the import twice does not add a task twice.

### Repeats

The repeat rules are in `decisions.md`. In short:

- A missed repeat does not pile up. Only the next one shows.
- Finishing early sets the next task from the due date, not from the day it was finished.
- Editing one changes only that one, unless `--all` is given.

A repeating task is one open task at a time. Finishing it marks it done and adds the next one.

## File format

The file is one JSON object with three keys.

| Key | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `version` | The format version, a whole number. It is 1. |
| `next_id` | The id the next new task gets. Ids are never used twice. |
| `tasks` | A list of tasks, oldest first. |

Each task is an object with these fields.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | whole number | The task's number. The commands and the page use it. |
| `title` | text | What to do. |
| `done` | true or false | True once the task is finished. |
| `due` | date or null | The day the task is due, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. There is no time of day. |
| `tags` | list of text | The task's tags, in lowercase, without the `#`, sorted. |
| `repeat` | text or null | `daily`, `weekly` or null. |

import os
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from unittest import mock

from jotdown.store import Store, new_data


class StoreTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        folder = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(folder.cleanup)
        self.path = Path(folder.name) / "data" / "tasks.json"

    def test_a_missing_file_is_a_new_list(self):
        self.assertEqual(Store(self.path).load(), new_data())

    def test_save_then_load(self):
        data = new_data()
        data["tasks"].append({"id": 1, "title": "renew passport"})
        Store(self.path).save(data)
        self.assertEqual(Store(self.path).load(), data)

    def test_save_replaces_the_old_file(self):
        store = Store(self.path)
        store.save(new_data())
        data = new_data()
        data["next_id"] = 5
        store.save(data)
        self.assertEqual(store.load()["next_id"], 5)

    def test_save_leaves_no_second_file_behind(self):
        Store(self.path).save(new_data())
        self.assertEqual([p.name for p in self.path.parent.iterdir()], ["tasks.json"])

    def test_text_outside_ascii_survives(self):
        data = new_data()
        data["tasks"].append({"id": 1, "title": "caf\u00e9"})
        Store(self.path).save(data)
        self.assertEqual(Store(self.path).load()["tasks"][0]["title"], "caf\u00e9")


class DataLocationTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """The store with no path given, as the jd command uses it. Runs in temporary folders only."""

    def setUp(self):
        folder = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(folder.cleanup)
        self.root = Path(folder.name)
        for name in ("home", "first", "other"):
            (self.root / name).mkdir()
        home = str(self.root / "home")
        environment = mock.patch.dict(os.environ, {"HOME": home, "USERPROFILE": home})
        environment.start()
        self.addCleanup(environment.stop)
        self.addCleanup(os.chdir, os.getcwd())
        os.chdir(self.root / "first")

    def test_tasks_saved_in_one_folder_are_found_from_another(self):
        data = new_data()
        data["tasks"].append({"id": 1, "title": "renew passport"})
        Store().save(data)
        os.chdir(self.root / "other")
        self.assertEqual(Store().load()["tasks"], data["tasks"])

# Jotdown design

Status: approved on 8 March 2027, with the reviewer's findings fixed.

## Purpose

Jotdown is a small task list for the command line and for a page in the browser. It is for its owner first and then for three friends, Sam, Priya and Leo, each on their own computer. Version 1 uses Python's standard library only.

## Scope

In version 1:

- tasks with a due date, tags and a daily or weekly repeat;
- commands to add, list, finish and edit tasks;
- a page in the browser that lists tasks, adds them and finishes them;
- a summary of late tasks and tasks due today, shown when the app opens;
- a one-time import of `my-todos.txt`.

Not in version 1: sharing or sync between people, a phone app, email reminders, and deleting tasks. To drop a task, finish it, or edit the file by hand.

## Words

The words are the ones in `glossary.md`: task, list, tag, tag group, due date and repeat. The commands, the page and the code use no other word for these things.

## Parts

### The store

The store reads and saves the list. The list is kept in one file, `~/.jotdown/tasks.json`: a `.jotdown` folder in the user's home folder, such as `/home/sam/.jotdown/tasks.json` or `C:\Users\Priya\.jotdown\tasks.json`. The folder the command runs in does not matter: every command and the page use this one file.

A save writes the whole list to a new file beside the old one, then renames the new file over the old one. A save that is cut off leaves the old file whole.

A missing file means a new, empty list. A file that exists but cannot be read as a list is an error: the store stops and says so. It never carries on with an empty list, because the next save would overwrite the file.

### The commands

The command is `jd`. With no command it shows the summary.

- `jd add TITLE`, with `--due`, `--tag` (more than once is fine) and `--repeat daily|weekly`.
- `jd list`, with `--tag` to show one tag group and `--done` to include finished tasks.
- `jd done ID` finishes a task.
- `jd edit ID`, with `--title`, `--due`, `--tag` and `--all`.
- `jd summary` shows what is late and what is due today.
- `jd import FILE` reads an old list.
- `jd web` starts the page.

### The page

`jd web` starts a page that listens on 127.0.0.1, the computer's own address, so only that computer can reach it. It shows the summary, lists the open tasks, adds a task from a form and finishes a task with a button. It uses `http.server` from the standard library.

### The import

`jd import FILE` reads a file such as `my-todos.txt`, one task per line. It takes `[ ]` and `[x]` at the start, a due date written as `(due YYYY-MM-DD)`, `#tags`, a weekday word such as `fri`, and the hints `every day`, `every week` and `every monday`. A line it cannot read as it is gets left out and listed with the reason. It never guesses. Running the import twice does not add a task twice.

### Repeats

The repeat rules are in `decisions.md`. In short:

- A missed repeat does not pile up. Only the next one shows.
- Finishing early sets the next task from the due date, not from the day it was finished.
- Editing one changes only that one, unless `--all` is given.

A repeating task is one open task at a time. Finishing it marks it done and adds the next one.

## File format

The file is one JSON object with three keys.

| Key | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `version` | The format version, a whole number. It is 1. |
| `next_id` | The id the next new task gets. Ids are never used twice. |
| `tasks` | A list of tasks, oldest first. |

Each task is an object with these fields.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | whole number | The task's number. The commands and the page use it. |
| `title` | text | What to do. |
| `done` | true or false | True once the task is finished. |
| `due` | date or null | The day the task is due, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. There is no time of day. |
| `tags` | list of text | The task's tags, in lowercase, without the `#`, sorted. |
| `repeat` | text or null | `daily`, `weekly` or null. |
| `scheduled` | date or null | For a repeating task: the date the repeat schedule gave this task. |
| `series` | object, optional | After one repeating task is edited alone: the `title` and `tags` the next task copies. |

An example with one task:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "next_id": 2,
  "tasks": [
    {
      "id": 1,
      "title": "renew passport",
      "done": false,
      "due": "2027-03-31",
      "tags": ["admin"],
      "repeat": null,
      "scheduled": null
    }
  ]
}
```

## How the parts connect

The commands and the page read and save through the store, and they share the same rules for tasks. The page reads the file for every request, so a task added with a command shows on the page at the next request.

## Main cases and failure paths

- Add a task, list it, finish it.
- Finish a task that repeats: the next one appears with the right due date.
- A save is cut off: the old file is still whole.
- The data file is broken by hand: every command and the page stop and say so, and the file is left as it is.
- Two saves at the same moment: the later one wins. Version 1 has no lock, and the command and the page are not meant to save at the same time.
- An import line cannot be read: it is left out and listed. The rest is imported.

## Decisions

- One JSON file. SQLite is set aside because not every Python is built with it. todo.txt is set aside because it has no standard field for repeats.
- The page listens on 127.0.0.1 only, so only the same computer can reach it.
- The summary is shown when the app opens. Nothing is sent by email or in any other way.
- Ids are whole numbers that are never used twice, so a task keeps its number.
- Tags are lowercase, so `Garden` and `garden` are one tag.
- The list lives in the home folder, at `~/.jotdown/tasks.json`, so every command finds the same file whatever folder it runs in. A path relative to that folder would give each folder a list of its own.

## Checks a builder can run

- `python3 -m unittest` passes.

- Run the commands from two different folders and open the page. All of them show the same tasks, kept in `~/.jotdown/tasks.json`.

# Jotdown design

Status: approved on 8 March 2027, with the reviewer's findings fixed.

## Purpose

Jotdown is a small task list for the command line and for a page in the browser. It is for its owner first and then for three friends, Sam, Priya and Leo, each on their own computer. Version 1 uses Python's standard library only.

## Scope

In version 1:

- tasks with a due date, tags and a daily or weekly repeat;
- commands to add, list, finish and edit tasks;
- a page in the browser that lists tasks, adds them and finishes them;
- a summary of late tasks and tasks due today, shown when the app opens;
- a one-time import of `my-todos.txt`.

Not in version 1: sharing or sync between people, a phone app, email reminders, and deleting tasks. To drop a task, finish it, or edit the file by hand.

## Words

The words are the ones in `glossary.md`: task, list, tag, tag group, due date and repeat. The commands, the page and the code use no other word for these things.

## Parts

### The store

The store reads and saves the list. The list is kept in one file, `~/.jotdown/tasks.json`: a `.jotdown` folder in the user's home folder, such as `/home/sam/.jotdown/tasks.json` or `C:\Users\Priya\.jotdown\tasks.json`. The folder the command runs in does not matter: every command and the page use this one file.

A save writes the whole list to a new file beside the old one, then renames the new file over the old one. A save that is cut off leaves the old file whole.

A missing file means a new, empty list. A file that exists but cannot be read as a list is an error: the store stops and says so. It never carries on with an empty list, because the next save would overwrite the file.

### The commands

The command is `jd`. With no command it shows the summary.

- `jd add TITLE`, with `--due`, `--tag` (more than once is fine) and `--repeat daily|weekly`.
- `jd list`, with `--tag` to show one tag group and `--done` to include finished tasks.
- `jd done ID` finishes a task.
- `jd edit ID`, with `--title`, `--due`, `--tag` and `--all`.
- `jd summary` shows what is late and what is due today.
- `jd import FILE` reads an old list.
- `jd web` starts the page.

### The page

`jd web` starts a page that listens on 127.0.0.1, the computer's own address, so only that computer can reach it. It shows the summary, lists the open tasks, adds a task from a form and finishes a task with a button. It uses `http.server` from the standard library.

### The import

`jd import FILE` reads a file such as `my-todos.txt`, one task per line. It takes `[ ]` and `[x]` at the start, a due date written as `(due YYYY-MM-DD)`, `#tags`, a weekday word such as `fri`, and the hints `every day`, `every week` and `every monday`. A line it cannot read as it is gets left out and listed with the reason. It never guesses. Running the import twice does not add a task twice.

### Repeats

The repeat rules are in `decisions.md`. In short:

- A missed repeat does not pile up. Only the next one shows.
- Finishing early sets the next task from the due date, not from the day it was finished.
- Editing one changes only that one, unless `--all` is given.

A repeating task is one open task at a time. Finishing it marks it done and adds the next one.

## File format

The file is one JSON object with three keys.

| Key | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `version` | The format version, a whole number. It is 1. |
| `next_id` | The id the next new task gets. Ids are never used twice. |
| `tasks` | A list of tasks, oldest first. |

Each task is an object with these fields.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | whole number | The task's number. The commands and the page use it. |
| `title` | text | What to do. |
| `done` | true or false | True once the task is finished. |
| `due` | date or null | The day the task is due, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. There is no time of day. |
| `tags` | list of text | The task's tags, in lowercase, without the `#`, sorted. |
| `repeat` | text or null | `daily`, `weekly` or null. |
| `scheduled` | date or null | For a repeating task: the date the repeat schedule gave this task. |
| `series` | object, optional | After one repeating task is edited alone: the `title` and `tags` the next task copies. |

An example with one task:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "next_id": 2,
  "tasks": [
    {
      "id": 1,
      "title": "renew passport",
      "done": false,
      "due": "2027-03-31",
      "tags": ["admin"],
      "repeat": null,
      "scheduled": null
    }
  ]
}
```

## How the parts connect

The commands and the page read and save through the store, and they share the same rules for tasks. The page reads the file for every request, so a task added with a command shows on the page at the next request.

## Main cases and failure paths

- Add a task, list it, finish it.
- Finish a task that repeats: the next one appears with the right due date.
- A save is cut off: the old file is still whole.
- The data file is broken by hand: every command and the page stop and say so, and the file is left as it is.
- Two saves at the same moment: the later one wins. Version 1 has no lock, and the command and the page are not meant to save at the same time.
- An import line cannot be read: it is left out and listed. The rest is imported.

## Decisions

- One JSON file. SQLite is set aside because not every Python is built with it. todo.txt is set aside because it has no standard field for repeats.
- The page listens on 127.0.0.1 only, so only the same computer can reach it.
- The summary is shown when the app opens. Nothing is sent by email or in any other way.
- Ids are whole numbers that are never used twice, so a task keeps its number.
- Tags are lowercase, so `Garden` and `garden` are one tag.
- The list lives in the home folder, at `~/.jotdown/tasks.json`, so every command finds the same file whatever folder it runs in. A path relative to that folder would give each folder a list of its own.

## Checks a builder can run

- `python3 -m unittest` passes.
- A save that is cut off leaves the old file whole: the new file is written first and renamed over the old one.
- Run the commands from two different folders and open the page. All of them show the same tasks, kept in `~/.jotdown/tasks.json`.
- Finish a daily task three days late: one new task, due today.
- Import `my-todos.txt`: every line is a task or is listed as left out.

## Open questions

- Whether the page and the commands need a lock if they are used at the same time.
- Whether Windows needs anything special for the data folder. It has not been tried.

import datetime
import io
import os
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from unittest import mock

from jotdown.cli import main
from jotdown.store import Store

TODAY = datetime.date(2027, 4, 12)  # a Monday


class CommandTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        folder = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(folder.cleanup)
        self.folder = Path(folder.name)
        self.store = Store(self.folder / "tasks.json")

    def jd(self, *argv):
        out, err = io.StringIO(), io.StringIO()
        status = main(list(argv), store=self.store, today=TODAY, out=out, err=err)
        return status, out.getvalue(), err.getvalue()

    def test_add_then_list(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.jd("add", "renew", "passport", "--due", "2027-04-20", "--tag", "admin")[0], 0)
        status, out, _ = self.jd("list")
        self.assertEqual(status, 0)
        self.assertIn("renew passport", out)
        self.assertIn("#admin", out)

    def test_a_due_date_can_be_a_plain_word(self):
        _, out, _ = self.jd("add", "call mum", "--due", "friday")
        self.assertIn("(due 2027-04-16)", out)

    def test_a_date_it_cannot_read_saves_nothing(self):
        status, _, err = self.jd("add", "call mum", "--due", "sometime soon")
        self.assertEqual(status, 1)
        self.assertTrue(err.startswith("jd: "))
        self.assertEqual(self.store.load()["tasks"], [])

    def test_list_can_show_one_tag_group(self):
        self.jd("add", "prune the roses", "--tag", "garden")
        self.jd("add", "call mum", "--tag", "family")
        _, out, _ = self.jd("list", "--tag", "garden")
        self.assertIn("prune the roses", out)
        self.assertNotIn("call mum", out)

    def test_an_empty_list_says_so(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.jd("list")[1], "No tasks.\n")

    def test_done_finishes_a_task(self):
        self.jd("add", "fix bike")
        status, out, _ = self.jd("done", "1")
        self.assertEqual(status, 0)
        self.assertIn("Done: [1] fix bike", out)
        self.assertEqual(self.jd("list")[1], "No tasks.\n")
        self.assertIn("x [1] fix bike", self.jd("list", "--done")[1])

    def test_done_on_a_task_that_does_not_exist(self):
        status, _, err = self.jd("done", "9")
        self.assertEqual(status, 1)
        self.assertIn("There is no task 9.", err)

        _, out, _ = self.jd("done", "1")
        self.assertIn("Next: [2] water the plants (due 2027-04-13)", out)

    def test_edit_changes_one_task(self):

        _, out, _ = self.jd("edit", "1", "--title", "fix the bike", "--due", "in 3 days")

"""The jd command."""
import argparse
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from jotdown import dates, importer, tasks, web
from jotdown.store import Store


def build_parser():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="jd", description="Jotdown: a small task list.")
    commands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command")

    commands.add_parser("summary", help="show what is late and what is due today")

    add = commands.add_parser("add", help="add a task")
    add.add_argument("title", nargs="+")
    add.add_argument("--due", help='a date such as friday, "in 3 days" or 2027-03-19')
    add.add_argument("--tag", action="append", default=[], help="a tag; repeat the option for more")
    add.add_argument("--repeat", choices=sorted(tasks.REPEAT_DAYS))

    show = commands.add_parser("list", help="show the open tasks")
    show.add_argument("--tag", help="show only the tasks with this tag")
    show.add_argument("--done", action="store_true", help="include finished tasks")

    done = commands.add_parser("done", help="finish a task")
    done.add_argument("id", type=int)

    edit = commands.add_parser("edit", help="change a task")
    edit.add_argument("id", type=int)
    edit.add_argument("--title")
    edit.add_argument("--due")
    edit.add_argument("--tag", action="append", help="the new tags; repeat the option for more")
    edit.add_argument("--all", action="store_true", dest="whole_series", help="change every task of a repeat")

    load = commands.add_parser("import", help="read an old list such as my-todos.txt")
    load.add_argument("file")

    page = commands.add_parser("web", help="start the page in the browser")
    page.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=web.DEFAULT_PORT)
    return parser


def cmd_summary(args, store, today, out):
    print("\n".join(tasks.summary_lines(store.load(), today)), file=out)
    return 0


def cmd_add(args, store, today, out):
    due = dates.parse_due(args.due, today) if args.due else None
    data = store.load()
    task = tasks.add_task(data, " ".join(args.title), due, args.tag, args.repeat, today)
    store.save(data)
    print(f"Added {tasks.format_task(task)}", file=out)
    return 0


def cmd_list(args, store, today, out):
    shown = tasks.visible_tasks(store.load(), args.tag, args.done)
    if not shown:
        print("No tasks.", file=out)
    for task in shown:
        print(("x " if task["done"] else "  ") + tasks.format_task(task), file=out)
    return 0


def cmd_done(args, store, today, out):
    data = store.load()
    task, following = tasks.finish_task(data, args.id, today)
    store.save(data)
    print(f"Done: {tasks.format_task(task)}", file=out)
    if following:
        print(f"Next: {tasks.format_task(following)}", file=out)
    return 0


def cmd_edit(args, store, today, out):
    due = dates.parse_due(args.due, today) if args.due else None
    data = store.load()
    task = tasks.edit_task(data, args.id, args.title, due, args.tag, args.whole_series)
    store.save(data)
    print(f"Changed {tasks.format_task(task)}", file=out)
    return 0


def cmd_import(args, store, today, out):
    data = store.load()
    try:
        added, skipped, rejected = importer.import_file(args.file, data, today)
    except OSError as error:
        raise tasks.TaskError(f"Cannot read {args.file}: {error.strerror}.") from None
    store.save(data)
    print(f"Imported {added} tasks. {skipped} were already in the list.", file=out)
    if rejected:
        print(f"{len(rejected)} lines were left out:", file=out)
        for number, line, reason in rejected:
            print(f"  line {number}: {line} ({reason})", file=out)
    return 0


def cmd_web(args, store, today, out):
    web.serve(store, args.port, out)
    return 0


COMMANDS = {
    "summary": cmd_summary,
    "add": cmd_add,
    "list": cmd_list,
    "done": cmd_done,
    "edit": cmd_edit,
    "import": cmd_import,
    "web": cmd_web,
}


def main(argv=None, store=None, today=None, out=None, err=None):
    """Run one command. Returns the exit status. The other arguments are for tests."""
    out = out or sys.stdout
    err = err or sys.stderr
    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
    store = store or Store(Path.home() / ".jotdown" / "tasks.json")
    today = today or dates.current_date()
    try:
        return COMMANDS[args.command or "summary"](args, store, today, out)
    except (tasks.TaskError, dates.DateError) as error:
        print(f"jd: {error}", file=err)
        return 1
