def visible_tasks(data, tag=None, include_done=False):
    """The tasks to show: open ones by default, soonest due first, tasks with no due date last."""
    shown = [t for t in data["tasks"] if include_done or not t["done"]]
    if tag:
        wanted = tag.lstrip("#").lower()
        shown = [t for t in shown if wanted in t["tags"]]
    return sorted(shown, key=lambda t: (t["due"] or "9999-99-99", t["id"]))


def format_task(task):
    parts = [f"[{task['id']}] {task['title']}"]
    if task["due"]:
        parts.append(f"(due {task['due']})")
    if task["tags"]:
        parts.append(" ".join("#" + tag for tag in task["tags"]))
    if task["repeat"]:
        parts.append(f"({task['repeat']})")
    return " ".join(parts)


# --- The opening summary ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def summary_lines(data, today):
    """The summary shown when the app opens: late tasks first, then the tasks due today."""
    iso = today.isoformat()  # ISO dates sort in date order as text
    open_tasks = [t for t in data["tasks"] if not t["done"] and t["due"]]
    past_due = sorted((t for t in open_tasks if t["due"] < iso), key=lambda t: (t["due"], t["id"]))
    due_today = [t for t in open_tasks if t["due"] == iso]
    if not past_due and not due_today:
        return ["Nothing is due today."]
    lines = []
    if past_due:
        lines.append("Overdue")
        lines.extend("  " + format_task(t) for t in past_due)
    if due_today:
        lines.append("Due today")
        lines.extend("  " + format_task(t) for t in due_today)
    return lines


# --- Importing an old list --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

CHECKBOX = re.compile(r"^\[([ xX])\]\s*")
DUE = re.compile(r"\(due\s+(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})\)")
TAG = re.compile(r"(?<!\S)#([\w-]+)")
DAYS = "monday|tuesday|wednesday|thursday|friday|saturday|sunday|mon|tue|wed|thu|fri|sat|sun"
EVERY = re.compile(rf"\b(?:every\s+(day|week|{DAYS})|(daily|weekly))\b", re.IGNORECASE)
WEEKDAY = re.compile(rf"\b({DAYS})\b", re.IGNORECASE)


class ImportLineError(Exception):
    """A line that cannot be taken as it is."""


def parse_line(line, today):
    """Read one line. Returns a dict with title, done, due, tags and repeat. Raises ImportLineError."""
    text = line.strip()
    done = False
    box = CHECKBOX.match(text)
    if box:
        done = box.group(1).lower() == "x"
        text = text[box.end():]
    due = None
    found = DUE.search(text)
    if found:
        try:
            due = parse_due(found.group(1), today)
        except DateError:
            raise ImportLineError(f"{found.group(1)} is not a real date") from None
        text = DUE.sub("", text)
    tags = TAG.findall(text)
    text = TAG.sub("", text)
    repeat = None
    every = EVERY.search(text)
    if every:
        word = (every.group(1) or every.group(2)).lower()
        repeat = "daily" if word in ("day", "daily") else "weekly"
        if word not in ("day", "week", "daily", "weekly") and due is None:
            due = parse_due(word, today)
        text = EVERY.sub("", text, count=1)
    weekday = WEEKDAY.search(text)
    if weekday and due is None:
        due = parse_due(weekday.group(1), today)
        text = WEEKDAY.sub("", text, count=1)
    title = " ".join(text.split())
    if not re.search(r"\w", title):
        raise ImportLineError("not a task")
    return {"title": title, "done": done, "due": due, "tags": tags, "repeat": repeat}


def import_text(text, data, today):
    """Add the readable lines to data. Returns (added, skipped, rejected).

    skipped counts lines whose task is already in the list, so a second import adds nothing.
    rejected holds (line number, line, reason) for each line that could not be read.
    """
    known = {(t["title"], t["due"]) for t in data["tasks"]}
    added = skipped = 0
    rejected = []
    for number, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), start=1):
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        try:
            fields = parse_line(line, today)
        except ImportLineError as error:
            rejected.append((number, line.strip(), str(error)))
            continue
        due = fields["due"]
        if fields["repeat"] and due is None:
            due = today  # a repeat needs a date to start from
        if (fields["title"], due.isoformat() if due else None) in known:
            skipped += 1
            continue
        task = add_task(data, fields["title"], due, fields["tags"], fields["repeat"], today)
        task["done"] = fields["done"]
        known.add((task["title"], task["due"]))
        added += 1
    return added, skipped, rejected


def import_file(path, data, today):
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        return import_text(f.read(), data, today)


# --- The commands -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def build_parser():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="jd", description="Jotdown: a small task list.")
    commands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command")

    commands.add_parser("summary", help="show what is late and what is due today")

    add = commands.add_parser("add", help="add a task")
    add.add_argument("title", nargs="+")
    add.add_argument("--due", help='a date such as friday, "in 3 days" or 2027-03-19')
    add.add_argument("--tag", action="append", default=[], help="a tag; repeat the option for more")
    add.add_argument("--repeat", choices=sorted(REPEAT_DAYS))

    show = commands.add_parser("list", help="show the open tasks")
    show.add_argument("--tag", help="show only the tasks with this tag")
    show.add_argument("--done", action="store_true", help="include finished tasks")

    done = commands.add_parser("done", help="finish a task")
    done.add_argument("id", type=int)

    edit = commands.add_parser("edit", help="change a task")
    edit.add_argument("id", type=int)
    edit.add_argument("--title")
    edit.add_argument("--due")
    edit.add_argument("--tag", action="append", help="the new tags; repeat the option for more")
    edit.add_argument("--all", action="store_true", dest="whole_series", help="change every task of a repeat")

    load = commands.add_parser("import", help="read an old list such as my-todos.txt")
    load.add_argument("file")

    page = commands.add_parser("web", help="start the page in the browser")
    page.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=8765)
    return parser


def cmd_summary(args, store, today, out):
    print("\n".join(summary_lines(store.load(), today)), file=out)
    return 0


def cmd_add(args, store, today, out):
    due = parse_due(args.due, today) if args.due else None
    data = store.load()
    task = add_task(data, " ".join(args.title), due, args.tag, args.repeat, today)
    store.save(data)
    print(f"Added {format_task(task)}", file=out)
    return 0


def cmd_list(args, store, today, out):
    shown = visible_tasks(store.load(), args.tag, args.done)
    if not shown:
        print("No tasks.", file=out)
    for task in shown:
        print(("x " if task["done"] else "  ") + format_task(task), file=out)
    return 0


def cmd_done(args, store, today, out):
    data = store.load()
    task, following = finish_task(data, args.id, today)
    store.save(data)
    print(f"Done: {format_task(task)}", file=out)
    if following:
        print(f"Next: {format_task(following)}", file=out)
    return 0


def cmd_edit(args, store, today, out):
    due = parse_due(args.due, today) if args.due else None
    data = store.load()
    task = edit_task(data, args.id, args.title, due, args.tag, args.whole_series)
    store.save(data)
    print(f"Changed {format_task(task)}", file=out)
    return 0


def cmd_import(args, store, today, out):
    data = store.load()
    try:
        added, skipped, rejected = import_file(args.file, data, today)
    except OSError as error:
        raise TaskError(f"Cannot read {args.file}: {error.strerror}.") from None
    store.save(data)
    print(f"Imported {added} tasks. {skipped} were already in the list.", file=out)
    if rejected:
        print(f"{len(rejected)} lines were left out:", file=out)
        for number, line, reason in rejected:
            print(f"  line {number}: {line} ({reason})", file=out)
    return 0


def cmd_web(args, store, today, out):
    from jotdown import web  # loaded only when the page is wanted, because web.py imports this module

    web.serve(store, args.port, out)
    return 0


COMMANDS = {
    "summary": cmd_summary,
    "add": cmd_add,
    "list": cmd_list,
    "done": cmd_done,
    "edit": cmd_edit,
    "import": cmd_import,
    "web": cmd_web,
}


def main(argv=None, store=None, today=None, out=None, err=None):
    """Run one command. Returns the exit status. The other arguments are for tests."""
    out = out or sys.stdout
    err = err or sys.stderr
    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
    store = store or Store()
    today = today or current_date()
    try:
        return COMMANDS[args.command or "summary"](args, store, today, out)
    except (TaskError, DateError) as error:
        print(f"jd: {error}", file=err)
        return 1
    except DataFileError as error:
        print(f"jd: {error}", file=err)
        return 2

import datetime
import unittest

from jotdown import cli
from jotdown.store import new_data

TODAY = datetime.date(2027, 4, 12)  # a Monday


class SummaryTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def data(self):
        data = new_data()
        cli.add_task(data, "pay council tax", datetime.date(2027, 4, 9), ["admin"])
        cli.add_task(data, "call mum", datetime.date(2027, 4, 12), ["family"])
        cli.add_task(data, "renew passport", datetime.date(2027, 4, 30))
        return data

    def test_nothing_due(self):
        self.assertEqual(cli.summary_lines(new_data(), TODAY), ["Nothing is due today."])

    def test_late_tasks_come_first_under_a_heading(self):
        lines = cli.summary_lines(self.data(), TODAY)
        self.assertEqual(lines[0], "Overdue")
        self.assertIn("pay council tax", lines[1])

    def test_tasks_due_today_come_next(self):
        lines = cli.summary_lines(self.data(), TODAY)
        self.assertEqual(lines[2], "Due today")
        self.assertIn("call mum", lines[3])

    def test_later_tasks_are_left_out(self):
        self.assertNotIn("renew passport", "\n".join(cli.summary_lines(self.data(), TODAY)))

    def test_finished_tasks_are_left_out(self):
        data = self.data()
        cli.finish_task(data, 1, TODAY)
        self.assertNotIn("pay council tax", "\n".join(cli.summary_lines(data, TODAY)))

    def test_a_repeating_task_that_was_missed_shows_once(self):
        data = new_data()
        cli.add_task(data, "water the plants", datetime.date(2027, 4, 5), repeat="daily", today=TODAY)
        lines = cli.summary_lines(data, TODAY)
        self.assertEqual(sum("water the plants" in line for line in lines), 1)

"""Jotdown's jd command and everything it needs, in one module."""
import argparse
import datetime
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from jotdown.store import DataFileError, Store

# tinydate is vendored. Find it from this file's own location, so it works from any folder.
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "vendor" / "tinydate"))

import tinydate


# --- Reading dates ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

class DateError(ValueError):
    """The text is not a date Jotdown can read."""


def current_date():
    return datetime.date.today()


def parse_due(text, today):
    """Return the date for text such as "friday", "in 3 days" or "2027-03-19"."""
    try:
        return tinydate.parse(text, today)
    except ValueError as error:
        raise DateError(str(error)) from None


# --- Tasks and the repeat rules ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

REPEAT_DAYS = {"daily": 1, "weekly": 7}


class TaskError(Exception):
    """The request cannot be done. The message says why."""


def clean_tags(tags):
    return sorted({tag.strip().lstrip("#").lower() for tag in tags if tag.strip().lstrip("#")})


def add_task(data, title, due=None, tags=(), repeat=None, today=None):
    """Add a task to data and return it. A repeating task without a due date is due today."""
    title = title.strip()
    if not title:
        raise TaskError("A task needs a title.")
    if repeat is not None and repeat not in REPEAT_DAYS:
        raise TaskError(f"A task cannot repeat {repeat!r}. Use daily or weekly.")
    if repeat and due is None:
        due = today or current_date()
    task = {
        "id": data["next_id"],
        "title": title,
        "done": False,
        "due": due.isoformat() if due else None,
        "tags": clean_tags(tags),
        "repeat": repeat,
        "scheduled": due.isoformat() if repeat else None,
    }
    data["next_id"] += 1
    data["tasks"].append(task)
    return task


def find_task(data, task_id):
    for task in data["tasks"]:
        if task["id"] == task_id:
            return task
    raise TaskError(f"There is no task {task_id}.")


def next_due(scheduled, repeat, today):
    """The next date a repeat falls on: counted from the scheduled date, and never in the past."""
    step = datetime.timedelta(days=REPEAT_DAYS[repeat])
    following = scheduled + step
    if following < today:
        # A missed repeat does not pile up. Jump to the first date on the schedule that is not past.
        missed = (today - following).days
        following += step * -(-missed // step.days)
    return following


def finish_task(data, task_id, today):
    """Mark a task done. A repeating task also gets its next task. Returns (task, next task or None)."""
    task = find_task(data, task_id)
    if task["done"]:
        raise TaskError(f"Task {task_id} is already done.")
    task["done"] = True
    if not task["repeat"]:
        return task, None
    scheduled = datetime.date.fromisoformat(task["scheduled"] or task["due"])
    following = next_due(scheduled, task["repeat"], today)
    series = task.get("series", task)
    new = add_task(data, series["title"], following, series["tags"], task["repeat"], today)
    return task, new


def edit_task(data, task_id, title=None, due=None, tags=None, whole_series=False):
    """Change a task. On a repeating task, the change is for this task only unless whole_series is true."""
    task = find_task(data, task_id)
    if task["done"]:
        raise TaskError(f"Task {task_id} is done. Edit the open one.")
    if title is None and due is None and tags is None:
        raise TaskError("Nothing to change. Give --title, --due or --tag.")
    if title is not None and not title.strip():
        raise TaskError("A task needs a title.")
    repeating = bool(task["repeat"])
    if repeating and not whole_series and (title is not None or tags is not None):
        # The next task is copied from the series, which this edit must not touch.
        task.setdefault("series", {"title": task["title"], "tags": list(task["tags"])})
    if title is not None:
        task["title"] = title.strip()
    if tags is not None:
        task["tags"] = clean_tags(tags)
    if due is not None:
        task["due"] = due.isoformat()
        if repeating and whole_series:
            task["scheduled"] = due.isoformat()
    if repeating and whole_series:
        task.pop("series", None)
    return task


def visible_tasks(data, tag=None, include_done=False):
    """The tasks to show: open ones by default, soonest due first, tasks with no due date last."""
    shown = [t for t in data["tasks"] if include_done or not t["done"]]
    if tag:
        wanted = tag.lstrip("#").lower()
        shown = [t for t in shown if wanted in t["tags"]]
    return sorted(shown, key=lambda t: (t["due"] or "9999-99-99", t["id"]))


def format_task(task):
    parts = [f"[{task['id']}] {task['title']}"]
    if task["due"]:
        parts.append(f"(due {task['due']})")
    if task["tags"]:
        parts.append(" ".join("#" + tag for tag in task["tags"]))
    if task["repeat"]:
        parts.append(f"({task['repeat']})")
    return " ".join(parts)


# --- The opening summary ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def summary_lines(data, today):
    """The summary shown when the app opens: late tasks first, then the tasks due today."""
    iso = today.isoformat()  # ISO dates sort in date order as text
    open_tasks = [t for t in data["tasks"] if not t["done"] and t["due"]]
    past_due = sorted((t for t in open_tasks if t["due"] < iso), key=lambda t: (t["due"], t["id"]))
    due_today = [t for t in open_tasks if t["due"] == iso]
    if not past_due and not due_today:
        return ["Nothing is due today."]
    lines = []
    if past_due:
        lines.append("Late")
        lines.extend("  " + format_task(t) for t in past_due)
    if due_today:
        lines.append("Due today")
        lines.extend("  " + format_task(t) for t in due_today)
    return lines


# --- Importing an old list --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

CHECKBOX = re.compile(r"^\[([ xX])\]\s*")
DUE = re.compile(r"\(due\s+(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})\)")
TAG = re.compile(r"(?<!\S)#([\w-]+)")
DAYS = "monday|tuesday|wednesday|thursday|friday|saturday|sunday|mon|tue|wed|thu|fri|sat|sun"
EVERY = re.compile(rf"\b(?:every\s+(day|week|{DAYS})|(daily|weekly))\b", re.IGNORECASE)
WEEKDAY = re.compile(rf"\b({DAYS})\b", re.IGNORECASE)


class ImportLineError(Exception):
    """A line that cannot be taken as it is."""


def parse_line(line, today):
    """Read one line. Returns a dict with title, done, due, tags and repeat. Raises ImportLineError."""
    text = line.strip()
    done = False
    box = CHECKBOX.match(text)
    if box:
        done = box.group(1).lower() == "x"
        text = text[box.end():]
    due = None
    found = DUE.search(text)
    if found:
        try:
            due = parse_due(found.group(1), today)
        except DateError:
            raise ImportLineError(f"{found.group(1)} is not a real date") from None
        text = DUE.sub("", text)
    tags = TAG.findall(text)
    text = TAG.sub("", text)
    repeat = None
    every = EVERY.search(text)
    if every:
        word = (every.group(1) or every.group(2)).lower()
        repeat = "daily" if word in ("day", "daily") else "weekly"
        if word not in ("day", "week", "daily", "weekly") and due is None:
            due = parse_due(word, today)
        text = EVERY.sub("", text, count=1)
    weekday = WEEKDAY.search(text)
    if weekday and due is None:
        due = parse_due(weekday.group(1), today)
        text = WEEKDAY.sub("", text, count=1)
    title = " ".join(text.split())
    if not re.search(r"\w", title):
        raise ImportLineError("not a task")
    return {"title": title, "done": done, "due": due, "tags": tags, "repeat": repeat}


def import_text(text, data, today):
    """Add the readable lines to data. Returns (added, skipped, rejected).

    skipped counts lines whose task is already in the list, so a second import adds nothing.
    rejected holds (line number, line, reason) for each line that could not be read.
    """
    known = {(t["title"], t["due"]) for t in data["tasks"]}
    added = skipped = 0
    rejected = []
    for number, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), start=1):
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        try:
            fields = parse_line(line, today)
        except ImportLineError as error:
            rejected.append((number, line.strip(), str(error)))
            continue
        due = fields["due"]
        if fields["repeat"] and due is None:
            due = today  # a repeat needs a date to start from
        if (fields["title"], due.isoformat() if due else None) in known:
            skipped += 1
            continue
        task = add_task(data, fields["title"], due, fields["tags"], fields["repeat"], today)
        task["done"] = fields["done"]
        known.add((task["title"], task["due"]))
        added += 1
    return added, skipped, rejected


def import_file(path, data, today):
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        return import_text(f.read(), data, today)


# --- The commands -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def build_parser():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="jd", description="Jotdown: a small task list.")
    commands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command")

    commands.add_parser("summary", help="show what is late and what is due today")

    add = commands.add_parser("add", help="add a task")
    add.add_argument("title", nargs="+")
    add.add_argument("--due", help='a date such as friday, "in 3 days" or 2027-03-19')
    add.add_argument("--tag", action="append", default=[], help="a tag; repeat the option for more")
    add.add_argument("--repeat", choices=sorted(REPEAT_DAYS))

    show = commands.add_parser("list", help="show the open tasks")
    show.add_argument("--tag", help="show only the tasks with this tag")
    show.add_argument("--done", action="store_true", help="include finished tasks")

    done = commands.add_parser("done", help="finish a task")
    done.add_argument("id", type=int)

    edit = commands.add_parser("edit", help="change a task")
    edit.add_argument("id", type=int)
    edit.add_argument("--title")
    edit.add_argument("--due")
    edit.add_argument("--tag", action="append", help="the new tags; repeat the option for more")
    edit.add_argument("--all", action="store_true", dest="whole_series", help="change every task of a repeat")

    load = commands.add_parser("import", help="read an old list such as my-todos.txt")
    load.add_argument("file")

    page = commands.add_parser("web", help="start the page in the browser")
    page.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=8765)
    return parser


def cmd_summary(args, store, today, out):
    print("\n".join(summary_lines(store.load(), today)), file=out)
    return 0


def cmd_add(args, store, today, out):
    due = parse_due(args.due, today) if args.due else None
    data = store.load()
    task = add_task(data, " ".join(args.title), due, args.tag, args.repeat, today)
    store.save(data)
    print(f"Added {format_task(task)}", file=out)
    return 0


def cmd_list(args, store, today, out):
    shown = visible_tasks(store.load(), args.tag, args.done)
    if not shown:
        print("No tasks.", file=out)
    for task in shown:
        print(("x " if task["done"] else "  ") + format_task(task), file=out)
    return 0


def cmd_done(args, store, today, out):
    data = store.load()
    task, following = finish_task(data, args.id, today)
    store.save(data)
    print(f"Done: {format_task(task)}", file=out)
    if following:
        print(f"Next: {format_task(following)}", file=out)
    return 0


def cmd_edit(args, store, today, out):
    due = parse_due(args.due, today) if args.due else None
    data = store.load()
    task = edit_task(data, args.id, args.title, due, args.tag, args.whole_series)
    store.save(data)
    print(f"Changed {format_task(task)}", file=out)
    return 0


def cmd_import(args, store, today, out):
    data = store.load()
    try:
        added, skipped, rejected = import_file(args.file, data, today)
    except OSError as error:
        raise TaskError(f"Cannot read {args.file}: {error.strerror}.") from None
    store.save(data)
    print(f"Imported {added} tasks. {skipped} were already in the list.", file=out)
    if rejected:
        print(f"{len(rejected)} lines were left out:", file=out)
        for number, line, reason in rejected:
            print(f"  line {number}: {line} ({reason})", file=out)
    return 0


def cmd_web(args, store, today, out):
    from jotdown import web  # loaded only when the page is wanted, because web.py imports this module

    web.serve(store, args.port, out)
    return 0


COMMANDS = {
    "summary": cmd_summary,
    "add": cmd_add,
    "list": cmd_list,
    "done": cmd_done,
    "edit": cmd_edit,
    "import": cmd_import,
    "web": cmd_web,
}


def main(argv=None, store=None, today=None, out=None, err=None):
    """Run one command. Returns the exit status. The other arguments are for tests."""
    out = out or sys.stdout
    err = err or sys.stderr
    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
    store = store or Store()
    today = today or current_date()
    try:
        return COMMANDS[args.command or "summary"](args, store, today, out)
    except (TaskError, DateError) as error:
        print(f"jd: {error}", file=err)
        return 1
    except DataFileError as error:
        print(f"jd: {error}", file=err)
        return 2

- `DESIGN.md`: the design and its decisions; for the file format it links to `docs/format.md`.
- `docs/install.md`: what you need, and how to start Jotdown.

- For: your friends, and you, to find the page that answers their question.

Gap and overlap check: after these changes the format and the data paragraph each have one home, every page under `docs/` is in the index, and nothing is in two places. `DESIGN.md`'s other sections, `CHANGELOG.md` and the code are not touched.

## Questions

### 1. Which is right for `due`?

Recommended answer: a date only, as in `docs/format.md` and the code. A time of day would need a code change, which is new work.

### 2. Make `docs/format.md` the one home of the format?

Recommended answer: yes, with `DESIGN.md` keeping a marked note that links there.

### 3. Give "Where your data lives" its one home in `docs/usage.md`, and fix the stale copy as above?

Recommended answer: yes. `README.md` and `docs/install.md` then link to it, and the old location goes.

### 4. Add the index as proposed?

Recommended answer: yes.

# Jotdown design

Status: approved on 8 March 2027, with the reviewer's findings fixed. Changed on 26 April 2027 to name where the data lives.

## Purpose

Jotdown is a small task list for the command line and for a page in the browser. It is for its owner first and then for three friends, Sam, Priya and Leo, each on their own computer. Version 1 uses Python's standard library only.

## Scope

In version 1:

- tasks with a due date, tags and a daily or weekly repeat;
- commands to add, list, finish and edit tasks;
- a page in the browser that lists tasks, adds them and finishes them;
- a summary of late tasks and tasks due today, shown when the app opens;
- a one-time import of `my-todos.txt`.

Not in version 1: sharing or sync between people, a phone app, email reminders, and deleting tasks. To drop a task, finish it, or edit the file by hand.

## Words

The words are the ones in `glossary.md`: task, list, tag, tag group, due date and repeat. The commands, the page and the code use no other word for these things.

## Parts

### The store

The store reads and saves the list. The list is kept in `~/.jotdown/tasks.json`, in the home folder, or in the file that the environment variable `JOTDOWN_DATA` names. The folder the command runs in does not matter.

A save writes the whole list to a new file beside the old one, then renames the new file over the old one. A save that is cut off leaves the old file whole.

A missing file means a new, empty list. A file that exists but cannot be read as a list is an error: the store stops and says so. It never carries on with an empty list, because the next save would overwrite the file.

### The commands

The command is `jd`. With no command it shows the summary.

- `jd add TITLE`, with `--due`, `--tag` (more than once is fine) and `--repeat daily|weekly`.
- `jd list`, with `--tag` to show one tag group and `--done` to include finished tasks.
- `jd done ID` finishes a task.
- `jd edit ID`, with `--title`, `--due`, `--tag` and `--all`.
- `jd summary` shows what is late and what is due today.
- `jd import FILE` reads an old list.
- `jd web` starts the page.

### The page

`jd web` starts a page that listens on 127.0.0.1, the computer's own address, so only that computer can reach it. It shows the summary, lists the open tasks, adds a task from a form and finishes a task with a button. It uses `http.server` from the standard library.

### The import

`jd import FILE` reads a file such as `my-todos.txt`, one task per line. It takes `[ ]` and `[x]` at the start, a due date written as `(due YYYY-MM-DD)`, `#tags`, a weekday word such as `fri`, and the hints `every day`, `every week` and `every monday`. A line it cannot read as it is gets left out and listed with the reason. It never guesses. Running the import twice does not add a task twice.

### Repeats

The repeat rules are in `decisions.md`. In short:

- A missed repeat does not pile up. Only the next one shows.
- Finishing early sets the next task from the due date, not from the day it was finished.
- Editing one changes only that one, unless `--all` is given.

A repeating task is one open task at a time. Finishing it marks it done and adds the next one.

## File format

> Moved on 3 May 2027 to [docs/format.md](docs/format.md), the one description of the file format. This section held the same tables and example, except that it gave `due` as a date and time (`YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM`). The code keeps `due` as a date, so the date-only form is the one kept.

## How the parts connect

The commands and the page read and save through the store, and they share the same rules for tasks. The page reads the file for every request, so a task added with a command shows on the page at the next request.

## Main cases and failure paths

- Add a task, list it, finish it.
- Finish a task that repeats: the next one appears with the right due date.
- A save is cut off: the old file is still whole.
- The data file is broken by hand: every command and the page stop and say so, and the file is left as it is.
- Two saves at the same moment: the later one wins. Version 1 has no lock, and the command and the page are not meant to save at the same time.
- An import line cannot be read: it is left out and listed. The rest is imported.

## Decisions

- One JSON file. SQLite is set aside because not every Python is built with it. todo.txt is set aside because it has no standard field for repeats.
- The page listens on 127.0.0.1 only, so only the same computer can reach it.
- The summary is shown when the app opens. Nothing is sent by email or in any other way.
- Ids are whole numbers that are never used twice, so a task keeps its number.
- Tags are lowercase, so `Garden` and `garden` are one tag.

## Checks a builder can run

- `python3 -m unittest` passes.
- A save that is cut off leaves the old file whole: the new file is written first and renamed over the old one.
- Run `jd` in two different folders. Both show the same list.
- Finish a daily task three days late: one new task, due today.
- Import `my-todos.txt`: every line is a task or is listed as left out.

## Open questions

- Whether the page and the commands need a lock if they are used at the same time.
- Whether Windows needs anything special for the data folder. It has not been tried.

# Jotdown design

Status: approved on 8 March 2027, with the reviewer's findings fixed. Changed on 26 April 2027 to name where the data lives.

## Purpose

Jotdown is a small task list for the command line and for a page in the browser. It is for its owner first and then for three friends, Sam, Priya and Leo, each on their own computer. Version 1 uses Python's standard library only.

## Scope

In version 1:

- tasks with a due date, tags and a daily or weekly repeat;
- commands to add, list, finish and edit tasks;
- a page in the browser that lists tasks, adds them and finishes them;
- a summary of late tasks and tasks due today, shown when the app opens;
- a one-time import of `my-todos.txt`.

Not in version 1: sharing or sync between people, a phone app, email reminders, and deleting tasks. To drop a task, finish it, or edit the file by hand.

## Words

The words are the ones in `glossary.md`: task, list, tag, tag group, due date and repeat. The commands, the page and the code use no other word for these things.

## Parts

### The store

The store reads and saves the list. The list is kept in `~/.jotdown/tasks.json`, in the home folder, or in the file that the environment variable `JOTDOWN_DATA` names. The folder the command runs in does not matter.

A save writes the whole list to a new file beside the old one, then renames the new file over the old one. A save that is cut off leaves the old file whole.

A missing file means a new, empty list. A file that exists but cannot be read as a list is an error: the store stops and says so. It never carries on with an empty list, because the next save would overwrite the file.

### The commands

The command is `jd`. With no command it shows the summary.

- `jd add TITLE`, with `--due`, `--tag` (more than once is fine) and `--repeat daily|weekly`.
- `jd list`, with `--tag` to show one tag group and `--done` to include finished tasks.
- `jd done ID` finishes a task.
- `jd edit ID`, with `--title`, `--due`, `--tag` and `--all`.
- `jd summary` shows what is late and what is due today.
- `jd import FILE` reads an old list.
- `jd web` starts the page.

### The page

`jd web` starts a page that listens on 127.0.0.1, the computer's own address, so only that computer can reach it. It shows the summary, lists the open tasks, adds a task from a form and finishes a task with a button. It uses `http.server` from the standard library.

### The import

`jd import FILE` reads a file such as `my-todos.txt`, one task per line. It takes `[ ]` and `[x]` at the start, a due date written as `(due YYYY-MM-DD)`, `#tags`, a weekday word such as `fri`, and the hints `every day`, `every week` and `every monday`. A line it cannot read as it is gets left out and listed with the reason. It never guesses. Running the import twice does not add a task twice.

### Repeats

The repeat rules are in `decisions.md`. In short:

- A missed repeat does not pile up. Only the next one shows.
- Finishing early sets the next task from the due date, not from the day it was finished.
- Editing one changes only that one, unless `--all` is given.

A repeating task is one open task at a time. Finishing it marks it done and adds the next one.

## File format

> Moved on 3 May 2027 to [docs/format.md](docs/format.md), the one description of the file format. This section held the same tables and example, except that it gave `due` as a date and time (`YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM`). The code keeps `due` as a date, so the date-only form is the one kept.

## How the parts connect

The commands and the page read and save through the store, and they share the same rules for tasks. The page reads the file for every request, so a task added with a command shows on the page at the next request.

## Main cases and failure paths

- Add a task, list it, finish it.
- Finish a task that repeats: the next one appears with the right due date.
- A save is cut off: the old file is still whole.
- The data file is broken by hand: every command and the page stop and say so, and the file is left as it is.
- Two saves at the same moment: the later one wins. Version 1 has no lock, and the command and the page are not meant to save at the same time.
- An import line cannot be read: it is left out and listed. The rest is imported.

## Decisions

- One JSON file. SQLite is set aside because not every Python is built with it. todo.txt is set aside because it has no standard field for repeats.
- The page listens on 127.0.0.1 only, so only the same computer can reach it.
- The summary is shown when the app opens. Nothing is sent by email or in any other way.
- Ids are whole numbers that are never used twice, so a task keeps its number.
- Tags are lowercase, so `Garden` and `garden` are one tag.

## Checks a builder can run

- `python3 -m unittest` passes.
- A save that is cut off leaves the old file whole: the new file is written first and renamed over the old one.
- Run `jd` in two different folders. Both show the same list.
- Finish a daily task three days late: one new task, due today.
- Import `my-todos.txt`: every line is a task or is listed as left out.

## Open questions

- Whether the page and the commands need a lock if they are used at the same time.
- Whether Windows needs anything special for the data folder. It has not been tried.

# Jotdown design

Status: approved on 8 March 2027, with the reviewer's findings fixed. Changed on 26 April 2027 to name where the data lives.

## Purpose

Jotdown is a small task list for the command line and for a page in the browser. It is for its owner first and then for three friends, Sam, Priya and Leo, each on their own computer. Version 1 uses Python's standard library only.

## Scope

In version 1:

- tasks with a due date, tags and a daily or weekly repeat;
- commands to add, list, finish and edit tasks;
- a page in the browser that lists tasks, adds them and finishes them;
- a summary of late tasks and tasks due today, shown when the app opens;
- a one-time import of `my-todos.txt`.

Not in version 1: sharing or sync between people, a phone app, email reminders, and deleting tasks. To drop a task, finish it, or edit the file by hand.

## Words

The words are the ones in `glossary.md`: task, list, tag, tag group, due date and repeat. The commands, the page and the code use no other word for these things.

## Parts

### The store

The store reads and saves the list. The list is kept in `~/.jotdown/tasks.json`, in the home folder, or in the file that the environment variable `JOTDOWN_DATA` names. The folder the command runs in does not matter.

A save writes the whole list to a new file beside the old one, then renames the new file over the old one. A save that is cut off leaves the old file whole.

A missing file means a new, empty list. A file that exists but cannot be read as a list is an error: the store stops and says so. It never carries on with an empty list, because the next save would overwrite the file.

### The commands

The command is `jd`. With no command it shows the summary.

- `jd add TITLE`, with `--due`, `--tag` (more than once is fine) and `--repeat daily|weekly`.
- `jd list`, with `--tag` to show one tag group and `--done` to include finished tasks.
- `jd done ID` finishes a task.
- `jd edit ID`, with `--title`, `--due`, `--tag` and `--all`.
- `jd summary` shows what is late and what is due today.
- `jd import FILE` reads an old list.
- `jd web` starts the page.

### The page

`jd web` starts a page that listens on 127.0.0.1, the computer's own address, so only that computer can reach it. It shows the summary, lists the open tasks, adds a task from a form and finishes a task with a button. It uses `http.server` from the standard library.

### The import

`jd import FILE` reads a file such as `my-todos.txt`, one task per line. It takes `[ ]` and `[x]` at the start, a due date written as `(due YYYY-MM-DD)`, `#tags`, a weekday word such as `fri`, and the hints `every day`, `every week` and `every monday`. A line it cannot read as it is gets left out and listed with the reason. It never guesses. Running the import twice does not add a task twice.

### Repeats

The repeat rules are in `decisions.md`. In short:

- A missed repeat does not pile up. Only the next one shows.
- Finishing early sets the next task from the due date, not from the day it was finished.
- Editing one changes only that one, unless `--all` is given.

A repeating task is one open task at a time. Finishing it marks it done and adds the next one.

## How the parts connect

The commands and the page read and save through the store, and they share the same rules for tasks. The page reads the file for every request, so a task added with a command shows on the page at the next request.

## Main cases and failure paths

- Add a task, list it, finish it.
- Finish a task that repeats: the next one appears with the right due date.
- A save is cut off: the old file is still whole.
- The data file is broken by hand: every command and the page stop and say so, and the file is left as it is.
- Two saves at the same moment: the later one wins. Version 1 has no lock, and the command and the page are not meant to save at the same time.
- An import line cannot be read: it is left out and listed. The rest is imported.

## Decisions

- One JSON file. SQLite is set aside because not every Python is built with it. todo.txt is set aside because it has no standard field for repeats.
- The page listens on 127.0.0.1 only, so only the same computer can reach it.
- The summary is shown when the app opens. Nothing is sent by email or in any other way.
- Ids are whole numbers that are never used twice, so a task keeps its number.
- Tags are lowercase, so `Garden` and `garden` are one tag.

## Checks a builder can run

- `python3 -m unittest` passes.
- A save that is cut off leaves the old file whole: the new file is written first and renamed over the old one.
- Run `jd` in two different folders. Both show the same list.
- Finish a daily task three days late: one new task, due today.
- Import `my-todos.txt`: every line is a task or is listed as left out.

## Open questions

- Whether the page and the commands need a lock if they are used at the same time.
- Whether Windows needs anything special for the data folder. It has not been tried.

# Jotdown

A small task list for the command line and for a page in your browser. It needs Python 3.12 or newer and nothing else.

## Install

Install Python 3.12 or newer, copy the Jotdown folder to your computer, and run `python3 -m jotdown` inside it. More in [docs/install.md](docs/install.md).

## Use

```text
jd add renew passport --due 2027-03-31 --tag admin
jd list
jd done 1
jd web
```

Run `jd` with no command to see what is late and what is due today. The commands are in [docs/usage.md](docs/usage.md), and the data file is described in [docs/format.md](docs/format.md). Where Jotdown keeps your tasks, and how to use another file: see [Where your data lives](docs/usage.md#where-your-data-lives). All the docs are listed in [docs/index.md](docs/index.md).

## Developer notes

- Run the tests with `python3 -m unittest` from the project folder. They use temporary folders and never touch your own tasks.
- `jotdown/cli.py` holds the commands, the reading of dates, the repeat rules, the summary and the import. `jotdown/store.py` reads and saves the file. `jotdown/web.py` is the page.
- `vendor/tinydate/` is a small date reader that Jotdown uses as it is.
- Standard library only. A new command is a function in `jotdown/cli.py` and an entry in its `COMMANDS` table.

## History of the design

Jotdown began as a shell script, `prototype/jot.sh`. The first design chose one JSON file over SQLite and todo.txt: JSON needs nothing to install, and not every Python is built with SQLite. A friend's Python turned out to have no `sqlite3` module, which confirmed the choice.

Version 0.4.0 moved the data file out of the working folder. Before that, two friends ran `jd` from a different folder and thought their tasks had vanished. The design had named `data/tasks.json` without saying what it was relative to.

## Changelog

### 0.4.0 - 2027-04-26

- The data file is now `~/.jotdown/tasks.json`, or the file that `JOTDOWN_DATA` names. It no longer depends on the folder you run `jd` from.
- A data file that cannot be read stops the command with a clear error. It is never overwritten.
- The page refuses requests that change tasks unless they come from the page itself.
- The commands, the date reading, the repeat rules, the summary and the import are in one module, `jotdown/cli.py`.

### 0.3.0 - 2027-03-15

- Importing an old list with `jd import`.
- Due dates in plain words, such as `friday` and `in 3 days`, through tinydate.

### 0.2.0 - 2027-03-15

- The page in the browser, started with `jd web`.

### 0.1.0 - 2027-03-15

- The store, the commands, daily and weekly repeats and the summary.

## Licence

Jotdown is released under the MIT licence.

# Using Jotdown

Run `jd` with a command. Run `jd` with no command to see the summary.

## The summary

When you run `jd` with no command, Jotdown shows the tasks that are late first, then the tasks that are due today, each group under its own heading. If nothing is late or due, it says so.

## Adding a task

```text
jd add renew passport --due 2027-03-31 --tag admin
```

A task has a title, and may have a due date, tags and a repeat. Give `--tag` more than once for more tags. Tags are lowercase, and a leading `#` is ignored.

## Dates

`--due` takes a date such as `2027-03-19`, and also plain words: `today`, `tomorrow`, a weekday name such as `friday` or `fri` (the next such day, never today) and `in 3 days`.

## Showing tasks

`jd list` shows the open tasks, soonest due first. Add `--tag garden` to show one tag group, or `--done` to include finished tasks.

## Repeats

`jd add water the plants --due today --repeat daily` adds a task that repeats every day. `--repeat weekly` repeats it every week.

- You only ever see one open task of a repeat. Finish it and the next one shows up.
- A missed repeat does not pile up. Only the next one shows.
- Finishing early sets the next one from the due date, not from the day you finished.
- Editing one changes only that one, unless you add `--all`.

## Finishing and editing

`jd done 3` finishes task 3. `jd edit 3 --title "call mum" --due friday` changes it. On a repeating task, `jd edit 3 --all --title "water the ferns"` changes every task of the repeat.

## The page

`jd web` starts a page in your browser at `http://127.0.0.1:8765/`. Only the computer it runs on can reach it. The page shows the summary and the open tasks, adds a task and finishes a task. It accepts those changes only from the page itself, not from other pages that your browser has open. Press Ctrl+C in the terminal to stop it.

## Where your data lives

Jotdown keeps your tasks in one file, `~/.jotdown/tasks.json`, in your home folder. It does not matter which folder you run `jd` from. To use another file, set the environment variable `JOTDOWN_DATA` to its path. Jotdown makes the folder and the file when you add your first task. Nobody else has a copy of this file, so copy it somewhere safe now and then.

# Jotdown

A small task list for the command line and for a page in your browser. It needs Python 3.12 or newer and nothing else.

## Install

You need Python 3.12 or newer. To check, run `python3 --version`, or `py --version` on Windows.

1. Copy the Jotdown folder to your computer and run `python3 -m jotdown` inside it.
2. To type `jd` in any folder, add `alias jd='PYTHONPATH=/path/to/jotdown python3 -m jotdown'` to `~/.bashrc` or `~/.zshrc`. On Windows, add a PowerShell function that sets `PYTHONPATH` and runs `py -m jotdown`.

Your tasks are kept in your home folder, in `~/.jotdown/tasks.json`, not in the Jotdown folder: see [Where your data lives](docs/usage.md#where-your-data-lives). To update, copy the new Jotdown folder over the old one; your tasks stay as they are. More in [docs/install.md](docs/install.md).

## Use

```text
jd add renew passport --due 2027-03-31 --tag admin
jd list
jd done 1
jd web
```

Run `jd` with no command to see what is late and what is due today. The commands are in [docs/usage.md](docs/usage.md), and the data file is described in [docs/format.md](docs/format.md). Where Jotdown keeps your tasks, and how to use another file: see [Where your data lives](docs/usage.md#where-your-data-lives). All the docs are listed in [docs/index.md](docs/index.md).

## Developer notes

- Run the tests with `python3 -m unittest` from the project folder. They use temporary folders and never touch your own tasks.
- `jotdown/cli.py` holds the commands, the reading of dates, the repeat rules, the summary and the import. `jotdown/store.py` reads and saves the file. `jotdown/web.py` is the page.
- `vendor/tinydate/` is a small date reader that Jotdown uses as it is.
- Standard library only. A new command is a function in `jotdown/cli.py` and an entry in its `COMMANDS` table.

## History of the design

Jotdown began as a shell script, `prototype/jot.sh`. The first design chose one JSON file over SQLite and todo.txt: JSON needs nothing to install, and not every Python is built with SQLite. A friend's Python turned out to have no `sqlite3` module, which confirmed the choice.

Version 0.4.0 moved the data file out of the working folder. Before that, two friends ran `jd` from a different folder and thought their tasks had vanished. The design had named `data/tasks.json` without saying what it was relative to.

## Changelog

### 0.4.0 - 2027-04-26

- The data file is now `~/.jotdown/tasks.json`, or the file that `JOTDOWN_DATA` names. It no longer depends on the folder you run `jd` from.
- A data file that cannot be read stops the command with a clear error. It is never overwritten.
- The page refuses requests that change tasks unless they come from the page itself.
- The commands, the date reading, the repeat rules, the summary and the import are in one module, `jotdown/cli.py`.

### 0.3.0 - 2027-03-15

- Importing an old list with `jd import`.
- Due dates in plain words, such as `friday` and `in 3 days`, through tinydate.

### 0.2.0 - 2027-03-15

- The page in the browser, started with `jd web`.

### 0.1.0 - 2027-03-15

- The store, the commands, daily and weekly repeats and the summary.

## Licence

Jotdown is released under the MIT licence.

# Jotdown

A small task list for the command line and for a page in your browser. It needs Python 3.12 or newer and nothing else.

## Install

Install Python 3.12 or newer, copy the Jotdown folder to your computer, and run `python3 -m jotdown` inside it. More in [docs/install.md](docs/install.md).

## Use

```text
jd add renew passport --due 2027-03-31 --tag admin
jd list
jd done 1
jd web
```

Run `jd` with no command to see what is late and what is due today. The commands are in [docs/usage.md](docs/usage.md), and the data file is described in [docs/format.md](docs/format.md). Where Jotdown keeps your tasks, and how to use another file: see [Where your data lives](docs/usage.md#where-your-data-lives). All the docs are listed in [docs/index.md](docs/index.md).

## More

- [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md)
- [Developer notes and the design's history](docs/development.md)

## Licence

Jotdown is released under the MIT licence.

# Developing Jotdown

## Developer notes

- Run the tests with `python3 -m unittest` from the project folder. They use temporary folders and never touch your own tasks.
- `jotdown/cli.py` holds the commands, the reading of dates, the repeat rules, the summary and the import. `jotdown/store.py` reads and saves the file. `jotdown/web.py` is the page.
- `vendor/tinydate/` is a small date reader that Jotdown uses as it is.
- Standard library only. A new command is a function in `jotdown/cli.py` and an entry in its `COMMANDS` table.

## History of the design

Jotdown began as a shell script, `prototype/jot.sh`. The first design chose one JSON file over SQLite and todo.txt: JSON needs nothing to install, and not every Python is built with SQLite. A friend's Python turned out to have no `sqlite3` module, which confirmed the choice.

Version 0.4.0 moved the data file out of the working folder. Before that, two friends ran `jd` from a different folder and thought their tasks had vanished. The design had named `data/tasks.json` without saying what it was relative to.

# Jotdown design

Status: approved on 8 March 2027, with the reviewer's findings fixed. Changed on 26 April 2027 to name where the data lives.

## Purpose

Jotdown is a small task list for the command line and for a page in the browser. It is for its owner first and then for three friends, Sam, Priya and Leo, each on their own computer. Version 1 uses Python's standard library only.

## Scope

In version 1:

- tasks with a due date, tags and a daily or weekly repeat;
- commands to add, list, finish and edit tasks;
- a page in the browser that lists tasks, adds them and finishes them;
- a summary of late tasks and tasks due today, shown when the app opens;
- a one-time import of `my-todos.txt`.

Not in version 1: sharing or sync between people, a phone app, email reminders, and deleting tasks. To drop a task, finish it, or edit the file by hand.

## Words

The words are the ones in `glossary.md`: task, list, tag, tag group, due date and repeat. The commands, the page and the code use no other word for these things.

## Parts

### The store

The store reads and saves the list. The list is kept in `~/.jotdown/tasks.json`, in the home folder, or in the file that the environment variable `JOTDOWN_DATA` names. The folder the command runs in does not matter.

A save writes the whole list to a new file beside the old one, then renames the new file over the old one. A save that is cut off leaves the old file whole.

A missing file means a new, empty list. A file that exists but cannot be read as a list is an error: the store stops and says so. It never carries on with an empty list, because the next save would overwrite the file.

### The commands

The command is `jd`. With no command it shows the summary.

- `jd add TITLE`, with `--due`, `--tag` (more than once is fine) and `--repeat daily|weekly`.
- `jd list`, with `--tag` to show one tag group and `--done` to include finished tasks.
- `jd done ID` finishes a task.
- `jd edit ID`, with `--title`, `--due`, `--tag` and `--all`.
- `jd summary` shows what is late and what is due today.
- `jd import FILE` reads an old list.
- `jd web` starts the page.

### The page

`jd web` starts a page that listens on 127.0.0.1, the computer's own address, so only that computer can reach it. It shows the summary, lists the open tasks, adds a task from a form and finishes a task with a button. It uses `http.server` from the standard library.

### The import

`jd import FILE` reads a file such as `my-todos.txt`, one task per line. It takes `[ ]` and `[x]` at the start, a due date written as `(due YYYY-MM-DD)`, `#tags`, a weekday word such as `fri`, and the hints `every day`, `every week` and `every monday`. A line it cannot read as it is gets left out and listed with the reason. It never guesses. Running the import twice does not add a task twice.

### Repeats

The repeat rules are in `decisions.md`. In short:

- A missed repeat does not pile up. Only the next one shows.
- Finishing early sets the next task from the due date, not from the day it was finished.
- Editing one changes only that one, unless `--all` is given.

A repeating task is one open task at a time. Finishing it marks it done and adds the next one.

## File format

> Moved on 3 May 2027 to [docs/format.md](docs/format.md), the one description of the file format. This section held the same tables and example, except that it gave `due` as a date and time (`YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM`). The code keeps `due` as a date, so the date-only form is the one kept.

## How the parts connect

The commands and the page read and save through the store, and they share the same rules for tasks. The page reads the file for every request, so a task added with a command shows on the page at the next request.

## Main cases and failure paths

- Add a task, list it, finish it.
- Finish a task that repeats: the next one appears with the right due date.
- A save is cut off: the old file is still whole.
- The data file is broken by hand: every command and the page stop and say so, and the file is left as it is.
- Two saves at the same moment: the later one wins. Version 1 has no lock, and the command and the page are not meant to save at the same time.
- An import line cannot be read: it is left out and listed. The rest is imported.

## Decisions

- One JSON file. SQLite is set aside because not every Python is built with it. todo.txt is set aside because it has no standard field for repeats.
- The page listens on 127.0.0.1 only, so only the same computer can reach it.
- The summary is shown when the app opens. Nothing is sent by email or in any other way.
- Ids are whole numbers that are never used twice, so a task keeps its number.
- Tags are lowercase, so `Garden` and `garden` are one tag.

## Checks a builder can run

- `python3 -m unittest` passes.
- A save that is cut off leaves the old file whole: the new file is written first and renamed over the old one.
- Run `jd` in two different folders. Both show the same list.
- Finish a daily task three days late: one new task, due today.
- Import `my-todos.txt`: every line is a task or is listed as left out.

## Open questions

- Whether the page and the commands need a lock if they are used at the same time.
- Whether Windows needs anything special for the data folder. It has not been tried.

# Jotdown

A small task list for the command line and for a page in your browser. It needs Python 3.12 or newer and nothing else.

## Install

Install Python 3.12 or newer, copy the Jotdown folder to your computer, and run `python3 -m jotdown` inside it. More in [docs/install.md](docs/install.md).

```text
jd add renew passport --due 2027-03-31 --tag admin
jd list
jd done 1
jd web
```

Run `jd` with no command to see what is late and what is due today. The commands are in [docs/usage.md](docs/usage.md), and the data file is described in [docs/format.md](docs/format.md). Where Jotdown keeps your tasks, and how to use another file: see [Where your data lives](docs/usage.md#where-your-data-lives). All the docs are listed in [docs/index.md](docs/index.md).

## Developer notes

- Run the tests with `python3 -m unittest` from the project folder. They use temporary folders and never touch your own tasks.
- `jotdown/cli.py` holds the commands, the reading of dates, the repeat rules, the summary and the import. `jotdown/store.py` reads and saves the file. `jotdown/web.py` is the page.
- `vendor/tinydate/` is a small date reader that Jotdown uses as it is.
- Standard library only. A new command is a function in `jotdown/cli.py` and an entry in its `COMMANDS` table.

## History of the design

Jotdown began as a shell script, `prototype/jot.sh`. The first design chose one JSON file over SQLite and todo.txt: JSON needs nothing to install, and not every Python is built with SQLite. A friend's Python turned out to have no `sqlite3` module, which confirmed the choice.

Version 0.4.0 moved the data file out of the working folder. Before that, two friends ran `jd` from a different folder and thought their tasks had vanished. The design had named `data/tasks.json` without saying what it was relative to.

## Changelog

### 0.4.0 - 2027-04-26

- The data file is now `~/.jotdown/tasks.json`, or the file that `JOTDOWN_DATA` names. It no longer depends on the folder you run `jd` from.
- A data file that cannot be read stops the command with a clear error. It is never overwritten.
- The page refuses requests that change tasks unless they come from the page itself.
- The commands, the date reading, the repeat rules, the summary and the import are in one module, `jotdown/cli.py`.

### 0.3.0 - 2027-03-15

- Importing an old list with `jd import`.
- Due dates in plain words, such as `friday` and `in 3 days`, through tinydate.

### 0.2.0 - 2027-03-15

- The page in the browser, started with `jd web`.

### 0.1.0 - 2027-03-15

- The store, the commands, daily and weekly repeats and the summary.

## Licence

Jotdown is released under the MIT licence.

# Using Jotdown

Run `jd` with a command. Run `jd` with no command to see the summary.

## The summary

When you run `jd` with no command, Jotdown shows the tasks that are late first, then the tasks that are due today, each group under its own heading. If nothing is late or due, it says so.

## Adding a task

```text
jd add renew passport --due 2027-03-31 --tag admin
```

A task has a title, and may have a due date, tags and a repeat. Give `--tag` more than once for more tags. Tags are lowercase, and a leading `#` is ignored.

## Dates

`--due` takes a date such as `2027-03-19`, and also plain words: `today`, `tomorrow`, a weekday name such as `friday` or `fri` (the next such day, never today) and `in 3 days`.

## Showing tasks

`jd list` shows the open tasks, soonest due first. Add `--tag garden` to show one tag group, or `--done` to include finished tasks.

## Repeats

`jd add water the plants --due today --repeat daily` adds a task that repeats every day. `--repeat weekly` repeats it every week.

- A repeating task is one open task at a time. When you finish it, the next one appears.
- A missed repeat does not pile up. Only the next one shows.
- Finishing early sets the next one from the due date, not from the day you finished.
- Editing one changes only that one, unless you add `--all`.

## Finishing and editing

`jd done 3` finishes task 3. `jd edit 3 --title "call mum" --due friday` changes it. On a repeating task, `jd edit 3 --all --title "water the ferns"` changes every task of the repeat.

## The page

`jd web` starts a page in your browser at `http://127.0.0.1:8765/`. Only the computer it runs on can reach it. The page shows the summary and the open tasks, adds a task and finishes a task. It accepts those changes only from the page itself, not from other pages that your browser has open. Press Ctrl+C in the terminal to stop it.

## Where your data lives

Jotdown keeps your tasks in one file, `~/.jotdown/tasks.json`, in your home folder. It does not matter which folder you run `jd` from. To use another file, set the environment variable `JOTDOWN_DATA` to its path. Jotdown makes the folder and the file when you add your first task. Nobody else has a copy of this file, so copy it somewhere safe now and then.

## Importing an old list

`jd import my-todos.txt` reads a file with one task per line: `[ ]` or `[x]` at the start, a due date written `(due 2027-03-31)`, `#tags`, a weekday word such as `fri`, and the hints `every day`, `every week` and `every monday`. A line it cannot read is left out and listed with the reason. Importing the same file twice adds nothing the second time.

# The data file format

Jotdown keeps the list in one JSON file. This page describes the file, for anyone who wants to edit it by hand or read it with another tool.

The file is one JSON object with three keys.

| Key | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `version` | The format version, a whole number. It is 1. |
| `next_id` | The id the next new task gets. Ids are never used twice. |
| `tasks` | A list of tasks, oldest first. |

Each task is an object with these fields.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | whole number | The task's number. The commands and the page use it. |
| `title` | text | What to do. |
| `done` | true or false | True once the task is finished. |
| `due` | date or null | The day the task is due, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. There is no time of day. |
| `tags` | list of text | The task's tags, in lowercase, without the `#`, sorted. |
| `repeat` | text or null | `daily`, `weekly` or null. |
| `scheduled` | date or null | For a repeating task: the date the repeat schedule gave this task. |
| `series` | object, optional | After one repeating task is edited alone: the `title` and `tags` the next task copies. |

An example with one task:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "next_id": 2,
  "tasks": [
    {
      "id": 1,
      "title": "renew passport",
      "done": false,
      "due": "2027-03-31",
      "tags": ["admin"],
      "repeat": null,
      "scheduled": null
    }
  ]
}
```

## Editing by hand

- Close the page and run no `jd` command while you edit.
- Keep `next_id` higher than every `id`.
- If the file stops being valid JSON, `jd` stops with an error and does not change it. Fix the file, or move it away to start a new list.

# Developing Jotdown

## Notes for developers

- Run the tests with `python3 -m unittest` from the project folder before every commit. They use temporary folders and never touch your own tasks.
- `jotdown/cli.py` holds the commands, the reading of dates, the repeat rules, the summary and the import. `jotdown/store.py` reads and saves the file. `jotdown/web.py` is the page.
- `vendor/tinydate/` is a small date reader that Jotdown uses as it is.
- Standard library only. A new command is a function in `jotdown/cli.py` and an entry in its `COMMANDS` table.
- `pip install -e .` from the project folder also gives a `jd` command, because `pyproject.toml` declares one.

## History of the design

Jotdown began as a shell script, `prototype/jot.sh`. The first design chose one JSON file over SQLite and todo.txt: JSON needs nothing to install, and not every Python is built with SQLite. A friend's Python turned out to have no `sqlite3` module, which confirmed the choice.

Version 0.4.0 moved the data file out of the working folder. Before that, two friends ran `jd` from a different folder and thought their tasks had vanished. The design had named `data/tasks.json` without saying what it was relative to.

# Jotdown 1.0.0

Released on 17 May 2027. The first release for the friends.

Jotdown needs Python 3.12 or newer and nothing else. To install it, follow the Install section of `README.md`.

## What it does

- The store, the commands, daily and weekly repeats and the summary.
- The page in the browser, started with `jd web`.
- Due dates in plain words, such as `friday` and `in 3 days`, through tinydate.
- Importing an old list with `jd import`.
- The summary heading for late tasks now reads Late.
- Docs for installing, using and developing Jotdown, with an index in `docs/index.md`. The file format is described once, in `docs/format.md`.

## Changed since the versions you tried

- The data file is now `~/.jotdown/tasks.json`, or the file that `JOTDOWN_DATA` names. It no longer depends on the folder you run `jd` from.
- A data file that cannot be read stops the command with a clear error. It is never overwritten.
- The page refuses requests that change tasks unless they come from the page itself.

Every change, version by version, is in `CHANGELOG.md`.
files_changed.README.md:
# Jotdown

A small task list for the command line and for a page in your browser. It needs Python 3.12 or newer and nothing else.

## Install

You need Python 3.12 or newer and nothing else. To check, run `python3 --version`. On Windows, run `py --version`.

1. Run `pip install jotdown`, or copy the Jotdown folder to your computer and open a terminal in it.
2. Run `python3 -m jotdown`. On Windows, run `py -m jotdown`. With no tasks yet it says that nothing is due today.
3. To type `jd` in any folder, make a shortcut that points at the Jotdown folder. [docs/install.md](docs/install.md) shows how on Linux, macOS and Windows.

To update, copy the new Jotdown folder over the old one. Your tasks are not in that folder, so they stay as they are.

## Use

```text
jd add renew passport --due 2027-03-31 --tag admin
jd list
jd done 1
jd web
```

Run `jd` with no command to see what is late and what is due today. All the docs are listed in [docs/index.md](docs/index.md).

Your tasks are kept in one file in your home folder. See [Where your data lives](docs/usage.md#where-your-data-lives).

## More

- [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md)
- [Developer notes and the design's history](docs/development.md)

## Licence

Jotdown is released under the MIT licence.

# Jotdown 1.0.0

Released on 17 May 2027. The first release for the friends.

Jotdown needs Python 3.12 or newer and nothing else. To install it, follow the Install section of `README.md`.

## What it does

- The store, the commands, daily and weekly repeats and the summary.
- The page in the browser, started with `jd web`.
- Due dates in plain words, such as `friday` and `in 3 days`, through tinydate.
- Importing an old list with `jd import`.
- The summary heading for late tasks now says Late.
- Docs for installing, using and developing Jotdown, with an index in `docs/index.md`. The file format is described once, in `docs/format.md`.

## Changed since the versions you tried

- The data file is now `~/.jotdown/tasks.json`, or the file that `JOTDOWN_DATA` names. It no longer depends on the folder you run `jd` from.
- A data file that cannot be read stops the command with a clear error. It is never overwritten.
- The page refuses requests that change tasks unless they come from the page itself.

Every change, version by version, is in `CHANGELOG.md`.

Written on 15 March 2027 for the agent that continues the work.

## Goal and state

Build Jotdown version 1 as `DESIGN.md` describes it, following `plan.md`. Steps 1 to 4 are built and the tests pass. The README's install section is written. Step 6, the friends, is next.

## Done so far

- The store, the commands and the page: `jotdown/`, with tests in `tests/`.
- The import of `my-todos.txt`: `data/tasks.json` holds 46 tasks. Two lines were left out, the separator `----` and `pay rent (due 2027-02-30)`. `my-todos.txt` now says where the list lives.
- Dates in plain words, through the vendored `vendor/tinydate/`.
- The README's install section is written.
- The test command `python3 -m unittest` passes.

## Decisions

All are in `decisions.md`, and the approved design is `DESIGN.md`. The repeat rules are in `decisions.md`.

## Remaining work

1. Step 6 of `plan.md`: a friend installs it.
2. The friends' answers to `questions-for-friends.md`, once the owner has them.
3. Next: delete prototype/.

## Open questions

- Whether the page and the commands need a lock if they are used at the same time: `DESIGN.md`, Open questions.
- Whether Windows needs anything special for the data folder.

## References

- `DESIGN.md`, `plan.md`, `decisions.md`, `glossary.md`, `questions-for-friends.md`, `AGENTS.md`.

## First next step

Ask the owner how the friends got on, and update `plan.md`.

## Written against

Branch main. All the work of 15 March is committed.

library.criterion: The visible “Going with” line, plus an offer of deep questions for parts whose answers depend on each other.
going with line and assumptions
The response, with its content, order and wording checked. There is no separate result.
The problem, goal, limits and test for a good answer, plus unknowns and what would settle them.
The requested options or candidates. Add a comparison and a decision, or why the choice is set aside, only when a choice was requested.
The response or Markdown material, laid out for its reader.

A comparison and recommendation, or no clear winner with what would settle it: the terms that matter, each option's values on the terms with its benefits, costs, risks and unknowns, the options dropped with reasons, why the recommended option beats the next best and how easily the choice can be undone, and the unknowns that would change it. Return options needing more development to the task that asked; do not start another brainstorm.

For an open name, the candidates, each with why it fits, or the chosen name and why. For a glossary change, the proposed entries. Add the rejected words with their reasons, and which existing terms and possible clashes you checked. Write or rename nothing here.
What was decided, set aside or passed to another task, with reasons. Include side topics and next steps; give the user the agreed summary.
decisions with reasons, parked questions with reasons, next steps and used methods results
The actual work and check results, task status, cost where needed and cleanup results.
Ranked findings with fixes, or a list of checks run when no problem was found. Mark unfinished checks. The design owner resolves findings before approval.

A short or full design with its actual approval status, such as "not yet approved", or ranked review findings. A full design also gives what its review found, how each finding was resolved, and any check still open.

Weak points that matter to the goal, including costs or risks even when success stays possible, each with its seriousness and remedy, then an honest verdict. When the user asked for the challenge, each assumption is marked checked or unchecked, and the most serious weakness comes first. When the challenge was not asked for, only the verdict and the serious weaknesses are shown, each with its reason, unless the user asks for more.
The earlier point, explained again to the user from the main idea to its details, with every reference in words.
The round of questions or the proposal, shown to the user, with the turn ended on it. When the user replies, each answer said back as accepted, changed, assumed or parked, by rule 4.
The summary of accepted, changed, assumed and parked items. The user has confirmed it, or got it in your final answer after telling you to start the work.
summary from the deep interview
The question document, in the response by default for the user to send. Later, return its answers to clarification.
questionnaire when applicable
The one-line or full plan, its actual approval status, and the checklist showing which steps were checked when execution was allowed. A full plan also shows what its challenge found.
The approved changes, the final pass over the whole, actual check results and unfinished work.
each claim with evidence, whether confirmed, and who checked it, with evidence beside the claim
A proposal with clear limits. After approval, return what was done and checked, or what was declined or still awaits approval.
The saved note with its actual review and approval status. On resuming, return the differences checked and the approved work that continues.
Each used method’s result and its actual status, returned to the task that asked for it.
What was removed, what was kept with its location and reason, and what still needs approval to remove.

The symptom, supported causes or marked hypotheses, rejected causes, and who should investigate or fix it next: the symptom with where, since when and how often it is seen; the chain from the symptom back to the trigger, each link with its evidence, confirmed or marked as a hypothesis; each cause ruled out with its evidence; and where a fix belongs, handed to the caller.
The worker’s starting instructions and the report it must return. The task that asked for the brief sends it; writing it starts no worker.
Combined findings, how they were combined and who checked them, their actual check status, sources and coverage limits.
The answer or claim verdict, supporting and opposing evidence, limits and missing checks.

Sourced findings and their limits: an answer or claim verdict, compared candidates, or evidence for possible causes, returned to the task that asked for the research. The limits include what was looked for and not found, what was not covered and why, and what would change the answer.
Each member’s answer with its name, a summary that keeps disagreements, and which answers are missing.

The risk level and a short reason, with the four answers or a “plainly low” judgment. When the user asked about the risk, they see the level and the four answers in plain words, unless it is plainly low. Otherwise the task that asked decides what the user needs to see.

The case, labelled one-sided: the precise position, reasons with their evidence and strength or marked as assumptions, the strongest objections each answered, conceded or met by narrowing, the weaknesses that still stand, how strong the case is and why, and the evidence that would strengthen or break it. The challenge's verdict is never part of the case.
Parts, their boundaries and each item’s place, with any placement still unresolved.

The grouping principle, each part’s boundary, each item’s place, and any missing or overlapping parts. After a change, also return the before-and-after map, checks, approvals and what was moved, changed or marked as replaced.
The view, how it will stay current and any requested tag edits. All other source content stays unchanged.
The combined account or proposal, a map of every original statement, updated references and items marked as replaced.
The shared part and working references to it. List copies with different meanings and leave them unchanged.

The material with missing parts added, and the gaps that could not be filled. The approval list gives each addition's source and reason, and each gap with what would settle it. The report after applying gives the result, its check and the gaps that remain.
The material with extra parts removed. The approval list gives each removal and why. The report after applying gives the result and its check.

The output or work plan fitted to its reader, with the point first. For reworked material, also return the list of changes for approval, then the result and its check once the list is applied. The sizing check itself stays in thinking.
The proposed or approved instruction document, its location and whether it was actually saved.
Approved lessons and where they were saved, highlights dropped with reasons, and decisions still waiting for the user.
